                                                                                    Events

                                                                                    Magnificent Men

                                                                                    May 2000

                                                                                    The airfield was just outside Saint-Avold, near Metz. Mordred pulled into the carpark at precisely nine o’clock, cursing under his breath. He’d planned to arrive a little earlier but traffic had been heavy after an accident on the A4. He hurried to make his appointment.

                                                                                    The man was waiting by one of the hangers. He wore a pair of overalls and gestured for Mordred to follow him inside and to the office at the side.

                                                                                    “Eugène Nungesser?”.

                                                                                    “Oui. And you would be Monsieur Marco. You are younger than I expected.”

                                                                                    Mordred’s eyes narrowed. “My family prefer not to waste time when it comes to our education.”

                                                                                    He was eyeing the day’s growth of stubble on Eugène’s chin and the tuxedo jacket hanging on the peg behind the door. Mordred hoped that his new teacher’s playboy lifestyle wasn’t going to get him killed.

                                                                                    The pilot quizzed Mordred on flight theory. This wasn’t a problem. Failing at this hurdle would very much disappoint his father.

                                                                                    After about half an hour, Nungesser seemed satisfied and led the way outside, towards a plane.

                                                                                    It was a Cessna 152, quite an old machine, not produced since the 80s, but it had a good reputation as a training vehicle.

                                                                                    The flight was exhilarating but exhausting. Eight hours of flying with short breaks for refuelling and lunch had taken their toll. Mordred stretched to relieve the stiffness after they landed that evening.

                                                                                    “Bon.” commented the instructor, “We’ll have you onto take-offs and landings in no time. Tonight though, we relax, I know some very nice bars in town.”

                                                                                    The bars were not to be their first stop. Nungesser pulled up outside an expensive-looking apartment block.

                                                                                    “My girlfriend’s place,” he explained, “I need to freshen up. Come on in.”

                                                                                    Inside, they found a man coiled up on one of the large sofas watching a football match on the television. He wore jeans and a t-shirt, so tight as to leave little to the imagination and almost room for a concealed weapon. Not that that meant the sofa wasn’t an excellent place to keep a blade or two.

                                                                                    “Ah, Charlie,” he greeted them without rising, “Bernardita said she would meet you at Café Jehanne d’Arc later. Who’s your friend?”

                                                                                    “César, this is Marco. For the next few weeks I’m giving him a grounding in flying, so to speak. Could you entertain him while I take a shower?”

                                                                                    The TV clicked off and the Spaniard eyed Mordred predatorily.

                                                                                    Nungesser decided that he’d spent long enough under the shower. Enough time for César to get Mordred into a vulnerable position and strike anyway. As he finished getting dressed and stepped out into the main room a cry of pain came from the young man’s en-suite. The pilot kicked the door down before things went too far.

                                                                                    He was confronted by the sight of a dripping Mordred pulling a jagged black dagger back to strike at César. The equally naked man was on the floor clutching his hand. It seemed to have an icicle, rapidly melting in the steamy bathroom, puncturing the palm.

                                                                                    “Don’t kill him! Sir. Mordred wanted me to test you. You passed.”

                                                                                    Mordred grunted. There wasn’t much to say to that. Just another reminder that his father saw him as a tool, discardable as soon as it lost its edge. He searched the bathroom cabinet for some antiseptic, which he found in a small first aid kit. He splashed some on the graze under his left arm where he hadn’t dodged out of the way quite fast enough.

                                                                                    “You stabbed me!”

                                                                                    Mordred’s heart sank. César was the type of sore looser who was going to indignantly point out the obvious. “Shocking that I’d do that when you had pulled a dagger from thin air and were aiming for my heart. That was a nice trick though.”

                                                                                    Nungesser was grinning. Mordred got the impression that he only tolerated César for the sake of his sister.

                                                                                    “Do you know who my father is?”

                                                                                    What a winey brat he was. Mordred flipped the dagger he’d taken in the air and caught it again. “No, but since you pulled a dagger with a boar’s head pommel from thin air, I’m going to hazard a guess that it’s Ares. Monsieur Nungesser said that this was a test on behalf of my father, so I doubt that Ares knows this is happening. How do you think he’d react if you went running to him after taking on a private contract, setting up a surprise attack, and then losing?! I think he’d be more upset with you than me to be honest.

                                                                                    “Now clean yourself up.” Mordred tossed the first aid box across to César, grabbed a towel and turned back to Nungesser. “How’s the wine at Café Jehanne d’Arc?”

                                                                                    The Frenchman’s grin grew broader.

                                                                                    See also:

                                                                                      Grigorievich’s Diamond

                                                                                      Aug 2002

                                                                                      On one of his first jobs for his father, Mordred was tasked to acquire a diamond from Aminev Boleslaw Grigorievich who was operating out of Berlin with a techno-grunge nightclub as a front. Things went rather wrong and Mordred found himself staring down the barrel of Grigorievich’s gun.

                                                                                      The crime boss, admittedly rather fuelled by his drinking earlier in the night, found the idea of Mordred turning up with a sword hilarious and ended up challenging him to a duel for the diamond. Pistol vs sword isn’t exactly fair, but when you’re starting at 50 paces in a dimly light night club with concrete pillars everywhere it is Mordred who has the advantage. Grigorievich lost sight of him the moment he dived behind the first pillar and didn’t manage to find him again until Mordred was behind him with a blade at his throat.

                                                                                      His lieutenant, Eckard Günzburg, didn’t appreciate his boss’ sign of weakness and tried to stab him in the back. Mordred saw him coming and quietly muttered “behind you” to Grigorievich causing him to spin and shoot Eckard in the chest. He gave Mordred the gun to thank him for saving his life.

                                                                                      Mordred keeps it, having had it deactivated, as a reminder that killing can be avoided, but that every choice has consequences.

                                                                                      See also:

                                                                                        The Ghost Of Philibert Aspairt

                                                                                        Nov 2003

                                                                                        During the French revolution, a doorman at the Val-de-Grâce hospital by the name of Philibert Apsairt got lost on the way to fetch a certain liqueur from a cellar and entered the Paris Catacombs instead. He never came out.

                                                                                        It wasn’t until 11 years later that his body was found, and only identified by the hospital keys on his belt. He was burred where they found him.

                                                                                        Every November 3rd, his spirit haunts his grave.

                                                                                        Two and a half centuries later, on that date, Mordred came looking for him, several bottles of good cognac and a pair of Urudanite goblets in hand.

                                                                                        When he found the spirit, they drank long into the night and Mordred found answers to the questions he had come with.

                                                                                        See also:

                                                                                          Diggy Diggy Parisian Hole

                                                                                          Nov 2003

                                                                                          Early in the afternoon of the 4th, Mordred woke with a nasty hangover and a back stiff from spending the night in a drunken stupor on the stone floor of the Paris Catacombs.

                                                                                          Dusting himself off, he followed Monsieur Aspairt’s directions until he heard dogs barking, or at least a recording of them. He could have avoided the security systems had he not wanted to be open about his presence.

                                                                                          “Glói”, Mordred called out before the folk ahead scattered, “I come peacefully, my father offers gold in exchange for your services.”

                                                                                          As he emerged into a room (complete with bar and projection screen) hewn out of the Catacombs, Mordred laid eyes on a dozen svartálfar braced to run or fight. He held his hands out to his sides, “Sir. Mordred has need of your special talents and is willing to pay handsomely for them.”

                                                                                          Mordred recognised the dwarf from the description he’d been given and locked eyes with him, “I’d like the opportunity to tell you about the project and negotiate a fair price, if you’re interested… and I have a couple of bottles of Martell Cordon Bleu cognac left.”

                                                                                          Glói’s eyes sparkled.

                                                                                            Farewell Albrecht

                                                                                            Feb 2006

                                                                                            “It’s raining.”

                                                                                            “It’s Scotland. In February. At two o’clock in the morning. Of course it’s raining.”

                                                                                            “Why am I here, Mordred?”

                                                                                            The car shock as the front driver’s side tyre hit a pothole. Morganette’s dagger bounced off the whetstone in her hand. Mordred felt a cold shiver run down his spine.

                                                                                            “Albrecht decided to hide out at an isolated little cottage in the middle of nowhere. This car plus his car is too many cars for me to drive away by myself.”

                                                                                            “And you couldn’t find one of your lowlife friends to help you out?”

                                                                                            “I don’t have any lowlife friends around Edinburgh. Father wants Albrecht dealt with immediately. There wasn’t any time for me to get a recommendation and vet someone.” Mordred glanced at his sister’s eyes in the rear-view mirror, unreadable. “I told Father I needed a driver we could trust. He sent you. I’m about as trilled as you clearly are.”

                                                                                            “You probably don’t even have the right address.”

                                                                                            Mordred suppressed a grimace. She was needling him. No need to rise to the bait. “I broke into his apartment in Munich and went though his post. Found a bank statement. He’s been using the cash machine in the village. I spent five minutes this afternoon posing as a German tourist needing directions. The barman was falling over himself to tell me about my reclusive countryman. He moved into Tomachlaggan Cottage and comes in to the shop once a week.”

                                                                                            The Tom Tom stuck to the windscreen emitted a bleep. They had reached their destination. Mordred let out a sigh as the end of the conversation neared. He killed the lights, gently pressed the brakes and slid the car around the corner. It was dark, so he judged the turning by the feel of the tyres crossing between the road and verge. The Ford Focus came to a halt with the lights of the cottage ahead.

                                                                                            “Shall we do this?” he asked.

                                                                                            “It’s raining, and you just needed someone to drive the car back.” The blade scraped across the whetstone again.

                                                                                            Mordred slowly breathed out. “Fine, wait for me just in case something unexpected crops up. I’ll be about half an hour.”

                                                                                            He opened the door and stepped out into the rain.

                                                                                            Albrecht was asleep in an armchair. The living room lights were out. The room was dimly lit by light leaking in from the kitchen and the glow of the television set. The man had drifted off watching something on Channel 5. The table beside him held an empty whisky bottle and a loaded pistol.

                                                                                            Mordred slid the pistol out of reach, paused to consider, and then moved the bottle next to it. From a pocket he pulled a garrotte and slipped it around the sleeping man’s neck. Albrecht awoke with a start as he started choking.

                                                                                            His arm flailed out, fruitlessly searching for the gun.

                                                                                            Mordred used his grip on the weapon to lift his victim out of the chair and dragged him towards the kitchen door.

                                                                                            Over Albrecht’s gurgles, Mordred whispered harshly in his ear. “You’re an idiot for double crossing Sir. Mordred and thinking you could get away with it. I don’t usually enjoy this kind of work, but considering what you did to those children, I’ll make an exception.”

                                                                                            The assassin pulled Albrecht through the kitchen and outside. The rain was getting heavier. It muted the smell when the German expired and his bowls relaxed.

                                                                                            Morganette watched him carry a human-sized bundle wrapped in a tarpaulin past the car. Mordred opened the boot and dropped his burden. There was a slight thump and a distinct bounce of the suspension.

                                                                                            “He drives a mini. Not a lot of room for a corpse in one of those.”

                                                                                            “So now you expect me to dispose of it?”

                                                                                            “Oh no, not you dear sister. How could I expect you to do any grunt work when you have me, your lowly brother to take care of it? There’s a pig farm three miles away, take it there. Its programmed into the satnav. I’ll do one more sweep of the cottage to make sure I haven’t missed anything. Then I’ll follow with his things and do the dirty work. When the landlord checks in on their tenant, they’ll assume that the mysterious and nervous German guy left as mysteriously and nervously as he arrived.”

                                                                                              Antonovich Elimination

                                                                                              Nov 2017

                                                                                              A few years ago, Mordred Sr. decided that a Russian general — Nikolai Antonovich — who was refusing to cooperate with his plans needed to be eliminated. He wanted it done quietly so Sr put together a team with his son, Mordred, as the trigger man.

                                                                                              Michelle Devereaux substituted herself for one of the team’s members before the first meeting and stayed undercover for the duration of the mission. As they spent three weeks setting up a situation where the general would be vulnerable, arranging for a group of Ukrainian militia to take the blame, and acquiring weapons that could be traced back to the Ukrainians, Michelle took the opportunity to become close to Mordred. After the assassination — a nice job at long range with a sniper rifle on an isolated road — the team celebrated.

                                                                                              Mordred Jr. and Michelle took the celebration back to his family estate where she was able to, while Jr was indisposed, get access to her real objective: Mordred Sr.’s study safe. Jr. doesn’t know what she took out of it or if it upset his father more or less than the loss of the bottle of Bowmore 1957 that they had drunk just prior to her heist.

                                                                                              Addendum: The item taken was a book. See The Romance of New York.

                                                                                              Addendum: Antonovich survived. See Matters of Trust.

                                                                                              Newt

                                                                                              Jan 2018

                                                                                              Where: Pinchvale

                                                                                              As Tuesdays went, it was pretty miserable. It was 5°C and drizzling. The rain assaulted Mordred’s collar as he left the grotty antique dealership — Mordred was sure he’d spotted a rat inside, not the sort of thing you want chomping on your century old furniture — and went back to his car, putting the package he was struggling with on the back seat.

                                                                                              Three days of tedious work had just come to an end. Three days of driving over half the country delivery messages and doing “shopping”.

                                                                                              Mordred was being punished for letting the thief into the castle. After a month of brutal “training” his father had grown board and told him to stay out of his sight. Now he’d moved on to treating his son as a dogsbody.

                                                                                              Three days out in Midgard without being expected to kill anyone, or even commit a crime. The younger Mordred was counting this as a win.

                                                                                              He reached the car just as the rain intensified. Now all that was left to do was to find the right balance of “contrite son” and “arrogant bastard”. He drove towards the pub he had seen earlier that afternoon; it was in walking distance of a hotel he could spend the night at.

                                                                                              He pulled into the pub’s car park. The car he thought might have been following him drove straight by. Visibility was still too poor to get a good look at it.

                                                                                              Dismissing his concerns as paranoia — he hadn’t done anything to attract attention — he dashed to the pub’s entrance, exchanged a glare with a crow perched nearby, ordered a pint and found a chair in the corner. It wasn’t as close to the roaring fire as he’d have liked, it was too busy an evening for that.

                                                                                              Mordred settled in with Identity Formation and Diversity in the Early Medieval Baltic and Beyond. It had arrived just in time for his trip and he’d been working his way through it for the past couple of evenings. It was the penultimate chapter — Swords from the Carolingian Empire to the Baltic Sea and Beyond — that had grabbed his attention and he’d resisted the urge to skip ahead.

                                                                                              “За здоровье!”, Mordred could tell he was slurring his words. That wasn’t a good sign. He’d had enough pints to have put his book away before the soldier had approached him — Seb was in civvies, but his bearing screaming military — and now, for reasons he couldn’t quite remember, there was a line of shots on the table between them.

                                                                                              This had probably been a mistake.

                                                                                              Mordred excused himself and, with a little exaggeration, rolled into the gent’s. He climbed into the sink and took a look at the window. It would be a tight squeeze, but he could fit through, but by the time he did Seb’s friend who’d carefully not been standing anywhere near them for the last two hours would be on him.

                                                                                              The other solider was standing in the rain smoking. The 2007 smoking ban had been a boon for people wanting an excuse to stand outside buildings and watch. There was something odd about the smoke, it wasn’t tobacco, or marijuana.

                                                                                              He considered trying to sneak out the main entrance. Too many people and too much alcohol.

                                                                                              ‘OK then. Figure out what they want. Brazen it out. Make them think I have the upper hand.’

                                                                                              The row of glasses had been refreshed.

                                                                                              “Oh, I’m an idiot.” Mordred was still just about coherent, but he’d been staring at the outline of a necklace — no, an amulet — around showing through the fabric of Seb’s t-shirt for the last two minutes.

                                                                                              It had been the final piece of the puzzle. The cigarette, the crow, the rat and the amulet.

                                                                                              “I’ve been asking myself what I did to draw the attention of a couple of druids, but it isn’t me you were interested in. It’s the antique dealer. Isn’t it?” Mordred watched Seb’s reactions. “Thought so. Hate to break it to you, I was just there to buy a painting. A previously unknown James Archer, it was going up for auction next month and I went in to pre… pre… to get there first. Course, it turned out to be a fake. Quite a good fake. I can see how it fooled the dealer. Would have been very embarrassing if it had got to the auction house. Public authentication? Nasty.

                                                                                              “Your turn now. What is that fellow up to that has you so interested?”

                                                                                              Seb cocked his head, “Any why should I explain my business to a Titanspawn?”

                                                                                              Mordred sighed inwardly, the crow could probably smell it or something, no point in denying it. “That, is discriminatory profiling.” he had to speak slowly to get the words out.

                                                                                              “But OK. You should explain your business because I might be able to help, I owe your subject nothing, and if I scratch your back now, then I can hope that you might return the favour in the future. I’ll even give you my oath that I’m not up to anything nefarious if you like.”

                                                                                              “And that’s worth something?”

                                                                                              “It’s not good to have a reputation as an oath-breaker.”

                                                                                              “Hard to measure a reputation without a name.”

                                                                                              “Mordred.”

                                                                                              “Wha…”

                                                                                              “Not that one. You think he does his own shopping? The old bastard is my father. Err. Pretend you didn’t hear that bit, the vodka is making me honest.”

                                                                                              “Agreed then. Your oath?”

                                                                                              “If we have a truce. No hurling me off to the glasshouse.”

                                                                                              “Agreed. Someone chopped down an oak tree. It belonged to a dryad.”

                                                                                              “It’s murder then?” asked Mordred.

                                                                                              “Her sisters are ready to go to war, but they don’t have a target and its going to get messy.”

                                                                                              “And Dryad-wood is valuable, and you think this antique dealer has it, but you aren’t sure and you don’t know where it is, so you can’t just tear the place apart looking for it?”

                                                                                              “Right.”

                                                                                              “Had you noticed how everything near the east wall is quite large, and not covered in the bric-à-brac that is the hallmark of the rest of the shop?”

                                                                                              Mordred had Seb’s attention.

                                                                                              “And that wall has everything fixed to it a little more firmly then the rest of the place? Because if I wanted to partition off a very private space to store things that shouldn’t be out in public, then … well … I’d hide it better than that. It’s just a guess, but I’d put money on it.”

                                                                                              Seb waved his companion over. “Get a couple of the lads to check for a partition in the east wall of the shop.”

                                                                                              “The alarm code is probably 1987.” Mordred chimed in.

                                                                                              The two soldiers stared at him.

                                                                                              “Those numbers are worn on the control panel, and it’s the year the shop was established. Says so on the sign outside. Now Seb, I’ve got two shots ahead while you’ve been staring. Keep up.”

                                                                                              There was definitely a hangover. And daylight. Too much daylight. The curtains were giving privacy but nothing more. The bed, and it was a bed, was firm. Mordred didn’t recognise the room.

                                                                                              Mordred glanced down. He was still wearing his suit. It was wrinkled. He stood up and checked the window. Not locked, first floor, overlooking a gravel driveway and some trees.

                                                                                              He tried the door, it wasn’t locked. The guard standing beside it turned to block his way, saluted and said, “I’ll let Captain Graves know you are awake, sir.”

                                                                                              Mordred returned the salute to give himself a moment to think. The guard was very young, unlikely to be a threat. He wasn’t here to keep Mordred there, it was a polite but formal request. Last night’s truce held.

                                                                                              “Very good.”

                                                                                              Mordred closed the door again and took another looked around the room.

                                                                                              There was a set of clean cloths folded on a chair. Khaki shirt, green wool trousers, and underwear. Officer’s service dress. No insignia. Someone had thoughtful raided the quartermaster’s stores in the middle of the night.

                                                                                              He showered and was just finishing getting dressed when there came a knock at the door. The insignia wasn’t a Captain’s.

                                                                                              “Good afternoon, Major”. His tone carried with it a hint of mockery.

                                                                                              “I am too hungover to be dealing with that sort of lip from a civilian, Mordred. They’re still serving lunch downstairs, can I offer you some?”

                                                                                              “Lead on.”

                                                                                              Lunch turned out to be buffet-service curry.

                                                                                              “Your information was spot-on. The dealer has been arrested, the wood recovered, and the dryads have been calmed sufficiently that we should have time to get the name of whomever sold the wood out of the prisoner.”

                                                                                              “Is that a thank-you?”

                                                                                              “It is.”

                                                                                              Mordred sucked air through his teeth, “Me doing favours for the other side. This had better not get out. I have a reputation to maintain.”

                                                                                              “You could build a new reputation. We could help.”

                                                                                              Mordred choked on a piece of chicken. “Are you asking me to defect?!”

                                                                                              “Interested?”

                                                                                              “You must be joking.”

                                                                                              “Hardly. You’re clearly skilled, unless last night was a ludicrously complicated scheme designed to win my trust, and you’ve got inside knowledge that could be useful. The files Captain Graves pulled last night made for interesting reading too. And I’ve got a good feeling about you.”

                                                                                              “And based on this feeling, you’re going to trust me?”

                                                                                              “I’m going to give you an opportunity to prove we can trust you.”

                                                                                              “Oh good. I thought you’d taken leave of your senses for a moment.” Mordred swallowed another mouthful. “It is an interesting offer, but files or no, I don’t think you really want my baggage. I know I don’t want my shoulder blades decorated with a dagger. So, I’ll have to say ‘no’.

                                                                                              “I’m happy to keep things friendly, it’s rare I can find someone who is good company and who can keep up with me at a bar, just not that friendly.”

                                                                                              See also:

                                                                                                Silver and the Scarab

                                                                                                May 2018

                                                                                                Spring was in the air, and Mordred was enjoying a few days of freedom before he was expected home. He’d spent the morning at the Louvre and was walking through the Champs-Élysées on his way to Christie’s.

                                                                                                Inside, he made a beeline to the item that had drawn him here. A rapier that one was, reportedly, the property of Charles-Geneviève-Louis-Auguste-André-Timothée d’Éon de Beaumont — better known as the Chevalier d’Éon.

                                                                                                “It’s a beautiful blade, is it not?”

                                                                                                The raven-haired woman with the Russian accent was right, it was double edged with two central fullers and an open swept hilt. Mordred crouched down to get a better look at the blade itself. Three fleur-de-lys armourer’s marks graced one side of it.

                                                                                                “It is indeed,” agreed Mordred, “and in excellent condition. I hadn’t heard of this until recently, it must have been in the owner’s family for quite some time.”

                                                                                                “Since 1760. It was given as a parting gift when Chevalier d’Éon departed St. Petersburg. It will be a shame to part with it, but needs must.”

                                                                                                “So you must be…”

                                                                                                “Pelageya Antonova.”

                                                                                                “A pleasure, although I’m sorry about the circumstances. Morton Red.” he offered her his card.

                                                                                                “You’re a collector?”

                                                                                                “Mostly a historian, although I do own a few interesting blades.”

                                                                                                Mordred circled the display case and couched back down to take a look at the other side. There was a tiny engraving that represented Secret du Roi — King Louis XV’s spy network. Few would notice it, fewer in the 18th century would understand it, but for those in the know it was a useful sign of allegiance.

                                                                                                “Very impressive.” he commented.

                                                                                                Something seemed off about it though. Mordred couldn’t put his finger on what. His concentration wasn’t helped by the fact he was being watched. The observer was about 5’8”, had short brown hair and was wearing a grey suit. Since Mordred had entered the room, the man had had his attention focused on the people and not the objects up for auction. He was probably some kind of security.

                                                                                                Today though, Mordred was here to bid and buy openly and honestly. The attention was a little disconcerting.

                                                                                                What was it about that mark on the blade that seemed so wrong?

                                                                                                Just as Mordred was thinking about going somewhere quiet to think and look up some details on his phone, his decision was made for him. SATT was here, two people he’d been warned about — Magician and Marco — and they were heading right for him, or the sword.

                                                                                                “I can’t monopolise your time though,” he said, turning away from the SATT operatives to face Antonova. “If you’ll excuse me?”

                                                                                                Mordred had locked himself in a cubicle in the gents’. It wasn’t the most dignified of positions to hunch over a phone screen and search through PDFs of academic papers in the hope of finding out what was bothering him, but it did the job.

                                                                                                He’s checked three sources and made sure that they weren’t cribbing from each other. The mark of the Secret du Roi was upside down. That meant it was either even more valuable then the estimate anticipated or it was a forgery.

                                                                                                Mordred dialed a number while he pulled out the brochure and checked the name of the seller.

                                                                                                “Kir old friend, sorry to bother you, but can you tell me anything about Pelageya Antonova?”

                                                                                                “A charming lady, she has an extensive collection of 18th century art, most of which has been in her family for generations. It is odd that you should ask about her now, I’m just on my way to meet her for dinner.”

                                                                                                “You’re in Paris?”

                                                                                                “Nyet, St. Petersburg. Morton, what have you gotten yourself into?”

                                                                                                “Nothing yet, I think I just came close to buying a nice forgery, but something smelt fishy and what you’ve told me certainly doesn’t make it any better. Tell your friend that she has an imposter selling art in her name in Paris, will you?”

                                                                                                “I will, and you must take me to dinner next time you’re in St. Petersburg.”

                                                                                                “Of course, Kir, of course. And thank-you.”

                                                                                                Mordred arrived back at the display room just in time to hear the grey-suited man announce:

                                                                                                “My name is John Silver, I’m with Hiscox Insurance, nobody is to leave this room until that sword is found.”

                                                                                                He had a raspy voice with a hint of a Cardiff accept buried under years of international travel.

                                                                                                The rapier was, indeed, absent. Something gold and blue glittered on the floor of the display case but Mordred couldn’t get a good look at it from the distance he was.

                                                                                                Silver’s eyes locked on Mordred. “You! I want a word with you.”

                                                                                                The office room was not as nice as the public areas of Christie’s and Mordred was trying not to roll his eyes in the face of the insurance man. He’d hit the limits of the man’s sense of humour about 30 seconds after they left the display room after Mordred made a crack about John Silver having lost his parrot.

                                                                                                “Let me see if I’ve got this straight. You think that I carefully examined the case containing the rapier, while drawing attention to myself by chatting up the seller and giving her my business card, left the room, made my way to the floor below, accessed the case from underneath, replaced the rapier with, what did you say it was?”

                                                                                                “A ceramic scarab.”

                                                                                                “… a ceramic scarab, secreted the sword somewhere, and then returned to the display room in some misguided attempt to give myself an alibi for ten minutes after the theft?”

                                                                                                “Yes!”

                                                                                                “Have you any idea how ridiculous that sounds?!”

                                                                                                Mordred thought he heard an amused grunt from the heavy standing outside the office door.

                                                                                                “You went into that room, spent longer looking at that sword than anyone else, and then left. Why?”

                                                                                                “Professional interest…”

                                                                                                “What is your profession?”

                                                                                                “I’m an academic. Do you read Historical Research? I had a good piece published in there last month. It’s about swords. A weapon belonging to the Chevalier d’Éon is very much my area of interest.” Silver seemed to be deflating. “And I left to find some peace and quiet to look something up, it made me pretty sure that sword is a forgery.”

                                                                                                “What?”

                                                                                                “You heard. If you want a report with my professional opinion then you can draw up a contract. I’m not going to get you off the hook for paying the insurance out of that sword for free, especially after you had me escorted out of there and then spent twenty minutes interrogating me. Shouldn’t you be out there looking for the real thief? Maybe talking to those gentlemen from the so-called counter-terrorist group?”

                                                                                                “What?” Silver was starting to sound like a stuck record.

                                                                                                Mordred gave descriptions of Magician and Marco. “They were pointed out to me a few years ago, they are supposed to work for some kind of secretive privately funded counter-terrorist organisation, but artifacts have an odd habit of disappearing when they are around. Could be coincidence. I’m not a thief, so that’s not my professional opinion.”

                                                                                                Silver growled. “Wait here. In fact…” he pulled out a pair of handcuffs and locked one end around Mordred’s wrist and the other around the radiator.

                                                                                                “Really?”

                                                                                                His only answer was the door slamming.

                                                                                                Mordred sighed. He could be gone in 30 seconds, even if he didn’t keep a handcuff key tucked into his ticket pocket. The second floor window opened out onto a wide ledge, it would probably be an easy climb. But that would raise questions about Morton Red.

                                                                                                He pulled out his phone and started to give the paper he had skimmed earlier a more thorough read.

                                                                                                Silver had not returned. The manager was apologising as Major in the Sûreté nationale unlocked the handcuffs. Mordred was being very forgiving, the last thing he wanted was to draw more attention, and using it as an opportunity to tout for business. Getting called in to authenticate weapons by Christie’s could provide some nice opportunities to learn about interesting blades before their going on sale become generally known.

                                                                                                The Poison Pen Affair

                                                                                                Aug 2021

                                                                                                When a scion of Zeus returned after a fifty year exile a party was held to celebrate. Vanessa said the team had to attend. During the party various pens were given as gifts. Greg received one (Berron and Alexia were there in a capacity as bodyguards rather than guests and did not).

                                                                                                The pens were marked with runes and enchanted so that their recipients did not want to give them up. When Greg’s was forcibly taken from him he became ill, and when Berron tried to destroy it it released poison gas into the area. It took some effort to heal those affected.

                                                                                                The Stonehenge Incident

                                                                                                Jan 2022

                                                                                                Typical. My first day at SATT and trouble hits; I wouldn’t put it past father to have timed his scheme to cause me maximum embarrassment.

                                                                                                Ophelia and I had just arrived and met Artie, Berron, Greg, and Maggie. Artie got a call about Magnus having just escaped an attack and Bad Moon being found dead with his heart ripped out.

                                                                                                Given two agents being under attack, and Alexia not being heard of for ‘ages’, Berron feared something might have happened to her so we — with the exception of Artie — went looking for Alexia at her home. We found signs of a struggle. Berron summoned a group of einherjar to search the grounds, while the rest of us established that Alexia was missing from the house.

                                                                                                I returned outside in an effort to work out where the attacking party came in. With the exception of the wheel marks of Berron’s vehicle, the driveway was pristine… up to the point where many foot and claw prints appeared. It seemed likely that a portal was used and Ophelia was able to brew a potion that allowed us to track it to Salisbury Plain.

                                                                                                Maggie was able to link the three people who had been attacked to an operation that resulted in the sorcerer Verdas being sealed up inside Porton Down. To follow up on this, I got in touch with Major Seb at Larkhill.

                                                                                                Getting into Larkhill itself was no trouble, but we — by which I mean Ophelia and myself — managed to upset a mystical security system around the officers’ mess which started wrapping us in vines and drew the attention of a group of soldiers. There was a lot of shouting, and Berron was more than ready to draw blood over the matter. I shall remain ever thankful for the invention of the mobile telephone as it allowed me to draw Seb outside the building to defuse the situation.

                                                                                                Inside, over drinks, we explained the situation and convinced Seb to get us inside Porton Down. He flashed an ID and we were waved inside; I’ve never had so little trouble getting inside a British military base. Senior SAS Druids are useful people to know.

                                                                                                On the way to Verdas’ chamber, I caught a glimpse of Michelle. It’s been a few years since I last saw her, but she is unmistakable. Later we’d learn that her reasons for being here were unconnected to ours, but that didn’t stop her plans interfering with ours.

                                                                                                Verdas’ chamber was littered with dead plants — not, I hasten to add, the kind that would make a druid cheerful if they were blooming — and a lectern that held what was left after the book that had been firmly fixed to it had been ripped away: Namely scraps of the leather (made from human skin) cover. Verdas himself had been banished to a pocket dimension so we attempted to establish if he was still trapped there. That was the moment that all hell broke loose.

                                                                                                First the doors locked and the lights went out: Michelle had finished her business and was making her escape while her distraction complicated our lives. Then the portal opened and harpies flooded through and attacked us. I hate harpies, they smell bad, have no table manners, and are far too good in a fight.

                                                                                                The resulting fight was painful, and mostly what I remember of it was being slammed against a wall whenever I thought I was going to land a blow on one of the enemy. The team did manage to bring them down, and stop the last one escaping through a portal using the Portal Gem it was carrying.

                                                                                                We were able to get the door unlocked, escape the room, and track down Michelle to confront her about her locking us in. That’s when we learned — Greg has a truth sense and could confirm the story — that it was pure coincidence. Michelle was delighted to see me. Berron attempted to flirt with her before discovering that she was one of his many sisters and became a little horrified instead. She decided to join us as we tracked the spell in the Portal Gem.

                                                                                                The Gem had all the hallmarks and personal style of father — I was not best pleased — and we were able to establish that it led to Jötunheimr, using Stonehenge to boost its power. We decided to take the fight to the enemy.

                                                                                                We arrived in the icy wasteland just in time to witness Alexia strapped to an altar about to be ritually murdered by a shadowy figure reading from a book with a tattered leather cover. The resulting fight saw the shadow man disappear — that’s the trouble with projections, they’re really hard to lock up, but I’m not taking any bets on his identity — his minions defeated, Alexia rescued, and the book sealed in ice.

                                                                                                Then it was just up to Ophelia to figure out a way to get us back to Midgard.

                                                                                                Back at HQ, Artie locked the book away in deep freeze citing the danger of it while we were unsure of the state of the containment of Verdas. I considered this to be a mistake, learning more details about what father was using the book for may have given us a lead on whatever his plan is.

                                                                                                With that option closed, I followed up with Alexia in the hope that she could remember some details about it from the first time she had encountered the plant sorcerer.

                                                                                                Alexia remembered the book but had thought it destroyed in an explosion during the original mission. She didn’t know much about it but remembered it had been used to summon creatures that attacked them. She promised to provide me with a copy of the field report. Alexia was also surprised that Artie had locked it away since he usually leaves such things to Maggie.

                                                                                                When I asked if he was usually that productive her exact words were “Oh gods no, generally he throws anything we find back at us unless he’s specifically sent us to retrieve something as his own filing system generally just loses things! I’ve tried to get him to tidy the system up but he usually just ends up sending us on missions to get me out of his way!”

                                                                                                We came to the conclusion that either the book was exceptionally dangerous but only now that Vardas had the possibility of escaping, or that his reasons for keeping it from the team were more to do with his trust of the team than the book itself. Somehow the attacker had identified the people involved in the original mission, which implies the possibility of a leak in SATT.

                                                                                                The mission also included team members named Click (also found dead) and Scarab who’s name has since been excised from the files — which suggests someone very high up is trying to hide the details of the mission after fearing a leak. Alexia hadn’t worked with him before or since that mission and hasn’t seen him in 6 months. He is a solo infiltration specialist so could be on a long undercover mission but Alexia suspects he is now either in great danger, dead, or the cause of the leak.

                                                                                                The team members on the original mission were, reportedly, all asked for specifically by Section 1.

                                                                                                Alexia mentioned there were a lot of folk tales about the archdruid — presumably Verdas — from a lot of different sources, and that any of those sources might lead to people who are willing to release him upon the world, but the knowledge of who was involved had to come from either the SATT reports or from the druid factions at Larkhill or Porton Down. The previous mission had involved Seb (a Captain at the time) who Alexia said was keen to stop Verdas.

                                                                                                Since I was planning on making a social call on one of the druids next week, I said I would see if I can uncover anything.

                                                                                                Alexia and I agreed to tell Artie what we were planning. Given what we suspect he suspects, sneaking around looking for information about Verdas behind his back would probably lead him to the wrong conclusions (as besides us then working across each other, it could be very unfortunate for me, personally). Alexia suggested he might also know who has the authority to edit the field reports.

                                                                                                The discussion we had with Artie led me to the conclusion that the problem is not isolated to the attempt to free Verdas. Details of the continued investigation can be found under the Mole Hunting event.

                                                                                                Seelie Coup

                                                                                                Jan 2022

                                                                                                Rumour states that SATT — including Alexia, Berron, Greg, and Maggie — lead a coup against Taranis and left the Seelie in a state of flux.

                                                                                                Section 1 seems to think Artie instigated it. Apparently it was Vanessa who had received an invitation for the group (which came sometime late in the organisation of the event) in recognition of the aid they had offered to the newly returned Princess Meredith, accepted it on behalf of the team, and then left it until two days before the event to tell them.

                                                                                                Mole Hunting

                                                                                                Jan 2022

                                                                                                Background: The events of the Stonehenge Incident led Alexia and me to the conclusion that something was rotten at SATT and it warranted looking into.

                                                                                                We paid Artie a visit. Alexia brought a Victoria sponge. His secretary summoned him like a naughty schoolboy to the headmaster’s office. He bought a Victoria sponge.

                                                                                                After a brief explanation of what we wanted, he took us to his office. The security around it is impressive. His stutter didn’t make it past the door.

                                                                                                Given Alexia had nearly been sacrificed Artie trusted her, and given I was new around here my involvement in the treachery seemed unlikely so he also extended his trust to me — while making it very clear that if I betrayed him I would regret it. I’d hoped to start out my relationship with grandfather on friendlier terms, and it is a shame that wasn’t to be, but not unexpected.

                                                                                                A brief summary of the highlights of the meeting:

                                                                                                • Whatever is going on must have been pulled off by someone at a senior level. The altered files — and they weren’t being altered by Artie to protect the agents mentioned in them — had been changed very cleanly. Aside from the missing names, they looked perfect with no sign of outright replacement or of magic, fey presence, or anything similar.
                                                                                                • The changes to the Verdas files are only the most recent example of a problem dating back at least five years.
                                                                                                • Scarab, the missing agent, had told Artie that his mother needed him. This is not unusual, and it he said that it isn’t unusual for the Egyptian gods to be bad about responding to requests for information. We probably don’t need to worry about him.
                                                                                                • Verdas’ book has been sent away to be looked after by someone Artie trusts
                                                                                                • Alexia and I can bring the rest of the team in on this problem

                                                                                                I’m still going to look at the Verdas incident from the druid angle, given the long running problem of SATT files being edited I’m even less inclined to think they had anything to do with the leak, but I do want to learn as much about Verdas as I can. If father wants to get his power, then I want to know why.

                                                                                                I’ll also see how much father trusts me these days and see if I can persuade him to let something useful slip.

                                                                                                Then Alexia and I will brief the team on what we’ve learned so far.

                                                                                                Romance of New York

                                                                                                Jan 2022

                                                                                                After running into Michelle during the Stonehenge Incident I asked her out. We’d been getting along quite well when we worked together and — lies, deceptions, and betrayals aside — I’d had a lot of fun. Since I was new in town, I invited her to surprise me.

                                                                                                I’ll confess. The delivery of an olive–green flight suit was a surprise. Since I wasn’t prepared to set tongues a–wagging by walking through the foyer of the Savoy wearing it, I tucked the box under one arm when I went downstairs to meet her.

                                                                                                Friday afternoon traffic on The Strand is not for the faint–hearted. It posed no challenge for Michelle though, the lights were always in her favour and every crowd of inattentive pedestrians had a car–sized gap in it.

                                                                                                We drove out of the city to a small airfield. The plane parked there was a model I didn’t recognise and had Wolf 2 splashed across the paintwork. The body was sleek, the engines massive, and I was pretty sure it was VTOL capable (I was right about that). Standing by it were a pair of women wearing flight suits that matched the one in the box I was holding. I assumed there were some of Michelle’s sisters.

                                                                                                Michelle led me into the building which was modern, bright, and every surface was covered in aeroplane parts. We, however, were just using it as a changing room.

                                                                                                We boarded the 4–seater and it rose into the air. The engine purred, and we soared. It was difficult to get a bearing from my position in the back, so it wasn’t until I was offered the pilot’s seat that I was able to check the systems and realise we were over the Atlantic — quite a long way over the Atlantic — but I didn’t have too long to stare at the instruments. Keeping the plane steady was challenging.

                                                                                                I’m hardly an expert pilot, most of my experience is with the Cessna 152, which I learned to fly for a job on Kefalonia some years back, and I only log a few more flight hours that I need to keep my license valid. This machine is not only of a different generation but a very different class. I wouldn’t have been able to handle some of the flight without Michelle on the co-pilot’s yoke.

                                                                                                Faster then I believed possible, we were landing at an airfield next to the Hudson. That jet was averaging almost Mach 1.5.

                                                                                                I generally avoid the US, its not a safe place to be given the activities of those Asclepius people, but we’d slipped in quietly and nobody was expecting us, so I wasn’t too concerned.

                                                                                                We were greeted with a speedboat and an instruction to hand it back to “Jonathan”. Michelle took the helm and guided us along the Hudson to a dockside restaurant called “By the Pier” where she was greeted by an older Italian-American man. He clearly knew her, and greeted her warmly as “Elizabeth”.

                                                                                                While he seemed to recognise a great many of his customers, we were the only table to get the personal touch. She mentioned that she had known his family for “a long time” and that the place got her out of Elliott’s bar.

                                                                                                There was a point in the evening where she told me she was glad I didn’t hold a grudge . I couldn’t really, she might have gotten one over me at the time, but I was just — more-or-less anyway — following father’s instructions so he was the real loser there. When I asked she said that the item she’d taken from the safe was a book. She teased me with promise of more details before becoming rather cold.

                                                                                                That was when the question of my loyalties came up. I was… evasive. It’s not a pleasant topic of conversation and it came rather unexpectedly. She seemed satisfied but I feel I should give her something concrete. That requires a lot of trust though, and that’s something I’ve not had much experience with.

                                                                                                We moved on to more pleasant topics only to be interrupted by a phone call. Michelle used the word “No” a lot, said that the shaft wouldn’t support it, that someone (a “him”) should be told “absolutely not that one”, and that the blueprint is ridiculous. She didn’t want to involve me, which was something of a shame as it sounded fascinating.

                                                                                                We moved on to a prohibition-style club nearby where there was whiskey (not bourbon, thankfully) and dancing. Michelle didn’t appear to be used to not taking the lead on the dance floor. I wasn’t sympathetic after the earlier blindsiding she gave me on loyalty.

                                                                                                We returned to the Savoy. For some reason, possibly the alcohol fumes coming off our breath, we weren’t invited to take the controls on the way home.

                                                                                                Whatever problem the shaft was causing, it continued to do so until Michelle turned her phone off — I think it had reached the point where she had to do either that or destroy it — at which point we enjoyed the rest of our night in peace.

                                                                                                She was gone by the morning, but sent breakfast. The champaign would have been better with company.

                                                                                                Turns out that “I’m new in town, you choose” didn’t get me the tour of interesting parts of London I was expecting.

                                                                                                Touring Salisbury Alehouses

                                                                                                Jan 2022

                                                                                                Seb took me to the Old Ale & Coffee House, it is an upmarket place with a deliberate rustic style. We caught up, over ale, and, at his prompting, we moved onto the matter that had been preying on my mind: Most of the Druids didn’t know who the team that took down Verdas was beyond being members of SATT which makes it unlikely the leak came from Seb’s end. Porton Down is even less likely to be the problem as the people there are kept intentionally dark about the nature of the demimonde.

                                                                                                The Druids aren’t particularly busy at the moment, there’s a situation in the east China seas that they are monitoring. Two gods are arguing over territory but the druids are keeping out of direct action. Seb offered their help resolving the current situation.

                                                                                                We moved back to more pleasurable topics along with The Haunch of Venison and The George and Dragon. Bets were made and the next morning saw us going at each other in full armour with blunted blades and stinking hangovers. It was a tie, and I hope that my head will stop ringing one day soon.

                                                                                                Visiting Family

                                                                                                Feb 2022

                                                                                                Since father seemed to be up to his neck in the Verdas business, I went to pay him a visit. I let Michelle and Alexia know where I was going in case things went pair-shaped and I needed a rescue.

                                                                                                At Alexia’s request I took a fire with me, a Bic lighter, which she played with to get a feel for it. She said it would let me contact her, and that I shouldn’t leave it too long before using it if I was in trouble. Of course, where I was going the difference between expected trouble and the deadly variety is a very find line to walk.

                                                                                                At the temple, the priestess opened a portal for me and I stepped through. The place was as hideous as ever (gold, silk, gold, pictures of father, gold, pictures of father killing Arthur (I think at least two were new in the last month), gold, marble, etc).

                                                                                                I followed the sound of sword on wood to the courtyard where father and Happy were warming up. I settled into the shadows to watch for a while as they started to spar. Happy, of course, is no match for father but I shouted out some words of encouragement as I stepped into the light and he managed to land a blow as father was distracted.

                                                                                                Morganette stepped out of the shadows behind me — she’s gotten much better in the few weeks that I’ve been away, surprisingly so as father doesn’t usually let any of us have that much power so quickly — and put a blade to my throat.

                                                                                                “Hello sister”, I responded. There was no point in being hostile, that wasn’t what I was here for.

                                                                                                She made me kneel before father and I went through the motions. Unlike her, I never really bought into the idea of him being a god, but I went through the motions. God or not, they were both capable of ending my life.

                                                                                                He dismissed Happy, and I gave my brother a wink when father’s back was turned.

                                                                                                I spun some half-truths about what I was up to. Taking the opportunity to infiltrate SATT as there was no chance of derailing the peace talks, but that SATT would be quite capable of being led into being the first to violate the ceasefire leaving us Titans with the moral high ground with the other factions.

                                                                                                Reaching an opportune moment for getting to my real purpose in coming here, I apologised for interfering with his plans for Verdas and he seemed genuinely baffled. He did mention that he had let Wally off the leash, and my elder brother always was a chip off the old block, so it seems that this might be his doing instead.

                                                                                                If so, then that makes things easier in some regards: Wally is formidable, but not on the same level as father. It does leave the problem of tracking him down though.

                                                                                                Father referred to Berron as Queen’s songbird, courtier to She Who Refused The Throne, Champion of the Axe. It wasn’t an epitaph I’d heard applied to him, but it seemed to fit.

                                                                                                He said that Sam had been very complimentary about me after the peace talks and that perhaps I wasn’t as useless as he thought. I’m really not sure what to make of this, it feels like a dangerous position to be in.

                                                                                                Father dismissed me after that, telling me to file a report and to do so again within the month. I did so, taking care to fill it with information that he’d already have access to along with a splash of personal colour.

                                                                                                Back at the Savoy, Michelle was waiting for me. Hotel door locks aren’t remotely a challenge for her. We chatted about family while I cleaned myself up after the trip. She mentioned that she’d avoided joining Berron, Alexia and her mother for dinner and we compared sisters. Michelle has lots but I have Morganette, it was something of a tie.

                                                                                                Meeting the Knight

                                                                                                Mar 2022
