                                                                                                We met in the SATT library with the intention of briefing the team on the situation with the altered files — there doesn’t appear to be any connection between them — and possible spy inside SATT.

                                                                                                Alexia, Berron and Greg went down to the armoury to check on the status of a particular snake totem that had disappeared from a report. They couldn’t find any record of it, nor could they find the physical item on the shelves.

                                                                                                Patrizia arrived with a message from Artie and said: “This is what Artie needs you to do, he is in one of his moods. Maggie, this is probably something you need books on Heraldry for.”

                                                                                                It said, in Artie’s handwriting: “I’ve got a small task for you. Someone was arrested on terrorism charges for the bomb on Oxford Circus, a mundane human thing. Check out the person in jail at Vauxhall nick. Ask for Detective Sally. The detainee has declined to give his name.”

                                                                                                Local news reports revealed that the MET had foiled a terrorist plot involving a home-made bomb at Oxford Circus and detained a suspect for questioning and showed an image of what they claimed was the suspect’s car; a surprisingly nice one for an accused terrorist. They didn’t have a picture of the suspect himself.

                                                                                                We went to the nick and found Sally Fields. Berron was shown in to talk to the suspect while the rest of us waited behind the one-way glass.

                                                                                                He was a rough, middle-aged man in a nice suit — at least it was before he’d slept in it in a cell — that matched the car for quality.

                                                                                                He said his name was Henry Watling and provided a few other details of his life and what he was doing around Oxford Circus (including a number of lies, according to Greg).

                                                                                                The Watling connection reminded me of the coat of arms of the knight in the picture in Artie’s office, and a quick message to Seb revealed that the Eternal Knight resided in Watling.

                                                                                                It was at that point a group of armed men in magic-absorbing kevlar burst into the police station. (This might have something to do with the Colani Gang, see the ongoing investigation)

                                                                                                We escaped through a portal opened by Alexia but not before Henry had been gunned down protecting Greg from a hail of bullets. He body disappeared.

                                                                                                Emerging in the SATT library, Maggie and I gave a quick run down on what we knew about the knight and she located his home in Watling. I showed Detective Fields out so she could get back to dealing with the problem at the station. Then we took a portal to Watling.

                                                                                                Henry lived in a National Trust property in Watling. Once we got past the point of being mistaken to tourists we were shown up to his study by Meredith (his assistant, priestess of Aphrodite or, as we later discovered, disguised False Mary)).

                                                                                                He was on the phone trying to arrange for a new car to replace the one taken into police custody at Oxford Circus. He was less than impressed at the suggestion he get a Maserati and insisted on an Aston Martin.

                                                                                                After dealing with introductions and him commenting that it had been a very long time since anyone called him Sir Knight and that we should call him Henry, he told us his story.

                                                                                                That was when the zombies started rising in the cellar. While we were dealing with them, hell-hounds attacked from the other direction. It was turning out to be one of those days.

                                                                                                The power to raise the zombies was coming through a hole, which I was able to plug with ice to step the tide and weaken the creatures while Henry and the others who weren’t dealing with the hounds were able to finish them off. It couldn’t stop them completely: Someone was fighting back, someone female. I suspected False Mary.

                                                                                                Meanwhile “Meredith” was in the process of stealing Henry’s freshly delivered new car and “persuading” Berron to come along with her.

                                                                                                Maggie, who knows Berron well enough to expect him to get lost, called up the tracker she had installed on his phone and we had a location of the stolen car.

                                                                                                We decided to catch Meredith in a pincer movement. Henry, Maggie and I followed in a Land Rover with the assistance of Jerry at TFL who was able to give us green lights and her red. It’s all very well having a flash sports car, but unless you’re willing to risk being T-boned at a cross-roads, you’re a slave to the traffic lights. I owe Jerry far too much good brandy.

                                                                                                The others took a portal to Alexia’s place to take her van and meet us coming in the other direction.

                                                                                                We followed Berron’s phone to Dormer’s Wells. A nice little part of West London.

                                                                                                Once we arrived we abandoned subtlety and just broke in through a couple of windows while Henry banged on the door to cause a distraction.

                                                                                                Cue fight. More of the kevlar goons, and False Mary herself. Who dissolved when Henry killed her.

                                                                                                Upstairs there was an alter which had been used for human sacrifice. It was clearly a used for sorcery and not dedicated to a deity or fiend, but it wasn’t clear what it was for. There were no spell books or writings to give us any further clues.

                                                                                                The cellar was full of bodies, including a fey that Berron decided needed returning to one of the Queens.

                                                                                                We called in Detective Fields as we suspected it would clear up a lot of missing persons cases.

                                                                                                Returning to SATT we tried to debrief Artie. He claimed to know nothing of the mission, and the note written in his handwriting had disappeared. This problem is getting worse.

                                                                                                Patrizia’s recollection of events tallied with ours, but she seemed confused about receiving cake. People are always giving her cake, why is she muttering about it now?

                                                                                                As we were about to go our separate ways for the evening Alexia got a message from Scarab: “He’s found me! Don’t trust…”.

                                                                                                So much for leaving him to his own devices.

                                                                                                See also:
                                                                                                • A Day in the Life

                                                                                                Breaking China

                                                                                                Apr 2022

                                                                                                A Dr. Aio asked for Greg and our help investigating a mysteriously collection of giant shells washing up on shore.

                                                                                                Artie arranged travel and told us Greg was in charge. Maggie, unimpressed at the prospect of travelling economy class (and given her unusual appearance I can’t blame her) arranged an upgrade to something with more comfort and privacy.

                                                                                                We were briefly mobbed by Colt Express fans on the way into the airport, but Berron distracted them before escaping with most of his clothes.

                                                                                                We flew into Qingdao where we were met by Min Kung Ming who took us to meet the doctor at her lab.

                                                                                                The sea shells appeared to be giant versions of western varieties that one wouldn’t usually expect to find in these seas. There was also giant seaweed which Ophelia struggled to identify. The most recent shells were deformed in strange ways that could not be natural.

                                                                                                Some searching by Maggie revealed some social media activity mentioning giant shells that was worth a follow up investigation.

                                                                                                We had hotel lodging in what was essentially a private house, which afforded us privacy. We took the opportunity to freshen up before going out to meet Sin Mai Otak at a sake bar.

                                                                                                I’d remembered Seb mentioning some trouble between a couple of gods around the Yellow Sea and wondered if there was a connection so I’d asked him to put me in touch with the local druid who had been keeping an eye on it.

                                                                                                The disagreement was between Mazu and Hebo. It seemed to be a territorial dispute over where the Yellow Sea met the Yellow River.

                                                                                                He suggested that the shells may have something to do with shèn which may have been summoned as mercenaries in the conflict.

                                                                                                The rest of the evening was passed gatecrashing a party held at the other end of the bar to celebrate the birth of a local man’s son.

                                                                                                Henry had been in the region in the late 1800s and wanted to revisit Liugong Island. This was one of the spots where the shells had been found (according to Maggie’s research). Ophelia, Maggie and I joined him there while Greg, Alexia, and Berron went to talk to the warring god and goddess.

                                                                                                Henry gave us a tour of the old navel base and the fishing village, which was surprisingly like 1950s Grimsby. The British influence here was plain.

                                                                                                He met a woman there who asked if he was there to take her home, and was disappointed when he did not understand her meaning. This was Arnemetia who had been there for around 120 years due to a barrier that prevents her from leaving.

                                                                                                We tracked down the people who had found the shell on the island. They’d turned the contents into soup. Happily it wasn’t harmful.

                                                                                                Meanwhile the rest of the team visited Mazu and Hebo. Both gods claimed that the other was the aggressor and Hebo revealed that was assured of this by Cocidius who also said that they were a weapon. A hawkish woman was leant against this throne, clearly highly placed in his circles.

                                                                                                Greg, being Greg, was easily able to determine which of these statements were lies and, when he more clearly identified himself caused Cocidius to flee.

                                                                                                We regrouped and exchanged what we had learned.

                                                                                                Before 1985, we realised, the island had been a somewhat different shape. It had been changed by bombardment from the Japanese navy. Somehow this had triggered a geomantic barrier that prevented Arnemetia’s departure.

                                                                                                It seems like too much of a coincidence to be chance, but there was no clue as to who might have had such a design in mind.

                                                                                                We returned to the island where we found Cocidius comforting Arnemetia. They revealed that there were married and Cocidius’s scheme to start a war between Hebo and Mazu was intended to break the island’s geomancy and free Arnemetia. She had run because she knew Greg’s reputation for stopping wars.

                                                                                                The giant shells were the product of an enlargement spell provided by a local witch. They were intended to trick Hebo into believing they were Shèn to provoke him.

                                                                                                Greg made use of his powers to break the shape of the island and free Arnemetia who immediately leapt into the ocean for the first time in over a century.

                                                                                                Cocidius did, at least, apologise for trying to start a war.

                                                                                                Ophelia wanted to visit the witch who turned out to be very much into the traditional sea-witch aesthetics (damp cave, eight limbs, etc.). She was somewhat peeved to discover the witch did not worship her mother.

                                                                                                I had been lurking closer to the entrance of the cave with the rest of the team who had little interest in meeting this witch, but that didn’t stop her approaching me and showing an irritating interest in my bloodline. I’ve never even met my grandmother.

                                                                                                Matters of Trust

                                                                                                Apr 2022

                                                                                                I took Michelle to meet Benny. This was a somewhat nerve-racking experience as she thought she’d helped me murder him some years ago. If she wasn’t all she seemed then this would be everything she’d need to convince my father to murder me.

                                                                                                On the way I warned her about her mother finding out about her plan for a girls’ night out. She wasn’t best pleased. She’d have been even less pleased if she’d turned up unexpectedly.

                                                                                                The introductions to Benny went well, although I did get something of an ‘explain yourself right now’ vibe coming from her. After relating the elaborate lengths we’d gone to to fake his death she seemed quite pleased. Now I just have to hope she doesn’t ever feel the need to have me killed, since I’ve loaded the gun for her.

                                                                                                Dinner was pleasant and we exchanged some more stories. She told me a little about her team.

                                                                                                I wished her well for her night with the girls and let her know how Henry and I were dragging her brother away from town so he wouldn’t be gatecrashing. I played for sympathy by telling how this distraction would involve wrapping ourselves in metal and hitting each other with sticks for which I was rewarded with a kiss. And then…

                                                                                                Assault on Froyle Park

                                                                                                Apr 2022

                                                                                                While the girls were out on the town, Henry, Berron, Seb, Greg and I retreated to Henry’s estate. Berron had caused enough trouble by telling his mother about the night out and I thought it best to distract him from any ideas about gatecrashing the party.

                                                                                                Henry’s idea of an afternoons entertainment involved jousting and alcohol. (I will not say which of Seb’s and Elliott’s mead was the better.)

                                                                                                After going to all the trouble to arrange for us to try to poke each other off horses with long sticks, Henry started making excuses about how it wouldn’t be fair for him to take part until I shamed him into mounting up.

                                                                                                Several shattered lances later, and Henry had defeated me. There was but a single point in it, so his claims of it being unfair were certainly disproved and we had shown the others just how it was done.

                                                                                                Berron smartly unseated Greg from his horse and promptly lost to Henry.

                                                                                                The afternoon proceeded pleasurably with food, drink and idle chatter.

                                                                                                And then came the knocking at the door.

                                                                                                To cut a long story short, three knights — one black, one green, and one blue — would take it in turns to knock, challenge whomever answered, and then fight until they had won (in which case they would march back out the gate) or lost (when they would vanish). Then the cycle would start again.

                                                                                                Meanwhile, a barrier of some kind had sprung up around the estate and we were unable to leave.

                                                                                                Greg and I hit the library to try to figure out what was going on. We found a couple of old stories about a trio of brothers who would show up at the home of someone who had wrong them. They were all killed but continued to return as ghosts until the family abandoned the home and left them to it.

                                                                                                Unfortunately, the barrier prevented us from leaving which made that option unavailable to us.

                                                                                                It was on leaving the library, which is a nasty dead spot for mobile signals that my phone starting screaming at me as it caught up with missed calls and messages.

                                                                                                The girls were in trouble (see the next entry). Unable to leave, I went through my address book and asked Michelle’s sisters, Elliott, and Detective Fields to help.

                                                                                                After a couple more rounds with the brothers while we tried to think of a way to deal with them — I suggested that giving them the vengeance they wanted and letting them kill Henry might do the trick, it wouldn’t be permanent after all, but that idea wasn’t very popular — we slipped out via faerie thanks to Berron’s contacts among the Unseelie.

                                                                                                Later, Henry, Ophelia and Alexia returned the same way to try to deal with the problem. Henry allowed himself to get stabbed, but it was realising that their true enemy was False Mary — after the mistook Ophelia for her — and convincing them that she had gone that did the trick.

                                                                                                See also:
                                                                                                • A Day in the Life

                                                                                                Night Out with the Girls

                                                                                                Apr 2022

                                                                                                While I was experiencing the questionable delights of wrapping myself up in steel and knocking Berron off a horse, and then being trapped in an Henry’s home by an invisible barrier, Michelle had taken the girls for a night out on the town (and been gatecrashed by her mother).

                                                                                                I haven’t had the full story yet, but from what I gather, the group was targeted because “Elizabeth” was present. They were drugged with something that suppressed their supernatural abilities. This did not please Freya.

                                                                                                By the time we had escaped from Froyle Park, they had managed to get Freya the antidote and Michelle’s Valkyrie sisters were raining down hell from above on the Printworks where they were being held.

                                                                                                Someone had turned the place into a secret underground fight club for the not-entirely human and completely inhuman to scrap it out and be gambled up on. Honestly, I’m a little disappointed that I didn’t get an invite.

                                                                                                There wasn’t really anything for us to do beyond watch the fireworks, and take joy in Michelle being unharmed.

                                                                                                That’s when one of the more uncomfortable experiences I’ve experienced happened. Imagine having your arms wrapped around a beautiful woman, lips locked against hers, the rest of the world disappearing in the moment … and then her mother noticing you. Now make that the first time you’ve met her mother. And now let her mother be Freya. Who has just finished dealing out bloody vengeance after being kidnapped.

                                                                                                I found myself having to deny luring Michelle away from whatever it was her mother had plans for. She is far too independent a women to need a man to set her on a path of her own.

                                                                                                Sally Fields arrived in response to my call and took charge of the clean up (dealing with things like asking Freya to keep out of the way of the cameras that had turned up).

                                                                                                Meanwhile Berron and Greg were raiding the remains of the Printworks’ office for paperwork. This led us to Justin Burland who had lost out of a couple of bids against “Elizabeth” recently.

                                                                                                Henry, Alexia and Ophelia returned to his home to take care of the brothers.

                                                                                                Some digging into Justin’s background revealed connections to Asclepius. His organisation had been kidnapping people on their behalf and delivering “shipments”. This seemed to end around the time that Asclepius were booted out of the UK by SATT, but it looked like he had taken what he had learned and taken advantage to set up the fight club (and likely some other business interests).

                                                                                                Maggie also managed to dig out he location (he was staying at the Savoy — the utter utter git: I really need to find my own place). The trick was to deal with him without causing a very public incident. Especially if that incident involved burning down a historic landmark where I was presently living.

                                                                                                Eventually, after much faffing about we cornered him in the Savoy gym (largely because just as we were about to head to his room, he left).

                                                                                                When confronted, Justin appeared extremely confused. His PA, on the other hand, did not. I hate it with the big corporate types turn out to not be the villain of the piece after all. It’s so enjoyable bringing them down.

                                                                                                Michael Blakemore turned out to be… formidable. He matched Berron in a fight before disappearing into the ventilation system. We split up and tried to coordinate the team around the lower floors of the hotel in order to corner him.

                                                                                                Sadly, that didn’t stop him shapeshifting into the form of a woman and slipping past us.

                                                                                                Maggie tracked his phone and Berron and I took chase on motorbike. It seemed too easy. It was too easy. We caught up with the black cab on Victoria Dock Road and found it empty aside from the drive and a bag containing the phone we were following and a notebook. Inside was a note addressed to Maggie:

                                                                                                I knew one of my sisters was in London. Didn’t know one would be so involved and would cause so much chaos. Well Done. It is time for you to come back into the fold. Father will expect it.

                                                                                                Your brother,

                                                                                                Michael.

                                                                                                With Michael in the wind, we headed back to regroup with the team, who were busily charging breakfast to my room, reading the latest news about Berron, and discovering that Vanessa had signed us up (on the recommendation of the Dragons to mediate some trouble at the Seelie Court.

                                                                                                See also:
                                                                                                • Watling, Henry

                                                                                                The Labyrinth of Chelmsford

                                                                                                Apr 2022

                                                                                                Artie sent us to investigate a minotaur sighting around the new storm drains of, of all places, Chelmsford.

                                                                                                Maggie hit social media and per usual and isolated the sighting to the town’s central park where we headed with orange high vis and a van (while Henry and Ophelia took his car and Berron hit motorbike).

                                                                                                There was something… odd about the storm drains near the sighting. There was some kind of distortion around them. That the minotaur has a historical affinity for labyrinths suggested this was the right place.

                                                                                                We proceeded inside with Alexia guarding our exit and Ophelia used a rapidly growing plant as a substitute for twine.

                                                                                                That didn’t stop the walls moving around us and cutting off our escape. Maggie and my efforts to hold it open were successful, but only for so long as we maintained the effort and that seemed to be a less useful application of our talents.

                                                                                                We have bought torches, but didn’t seem to need them. The walls were covered in luminescent moss (Ophelia collected a sample).

                                                                                                That was when the plant went limp, cut off from where we had started and removing the need to Alexia to keep an eye on its far end. She attempted to portal to our location, but something diverted her off course and she ended up in another part of the labyrinth.

                                                                                                Berron strode off looking for her. You’d think that he might accept that in a place where the walls move and portals get diverted that it might be useful to apply a bit of brain to the problem, but no.

                                                                                                There was giggling from up ahead and he ran into a pair of goblins. After he had applied his charm to them we quickly learned that there were no ordinary goblins. They didn’t speak the language of typical Fae creatures, preferring modern English, dressed as fantasy adventurers, served and feared The Dark Lord, and had no concept of time or hunger (which didn’t stop them rapidly getting addicted to the sugary fruit bars that Berron fed them while claiming to be a Light Lord). Their names were Snick and Snack.

                                                                                                They were able to give us some idea of what to expect along the way, and Berron was able to bribe them into facing up to their fear of the Dark Lord by bribing them with sugar. It seemed rather cruel.

                                                                                                This place was starting to feel decidedly unreal.

                                                                                                Meanwhile Alexia found what appeared to be a combination of a blacksmithery and a teenager’s lair (down to a collection of snacks and a D&D magazine).

                                                                                                The rest of us had followed the directions given by the goblins and come across a corridor beset by swinging axes. I froze one in place while Maggie calculated the timing of the others and crossed to the other side where the switch that disabled them was.

                                                                                                Berron waved the wrapper of one of his fruit bars across one of the blades. It was very sharp.

                                                                                                On the other side was a scroll that congratulated us on passing level one and challenging us to go to level 2. There was a well. I climbed down it first.

                                                                                                Level 2 was lit by flaming torches in sconces. The room we were in was tiled with various symbols on the tiles. Alexia found a similar puzzle in the magazine she had stumbled across — that this place was conjured from imagination was increasingly likely.

                                                                                                We crossed, stepping on the wheat symbols that matches the loaf of bread we could see on the other wise.

                                                                                                Once more there was a scroll and a well and level 3.

                                                                                                Imagination being, it seemed, a little on the limited side, level 3 was back to the glowing green moss for lighting.

                                                                                                Here there was a pool, with handholds on the walls and bars to swing across on the ceiling.

                                                                                                The water looked lovely. Alexia’s magazine suggested it was either full or flesh eating piranhas or highly acidic. Ophelia’s test showed it to be the latter as her litmus paper rapidly dissolved in the liquid.

                                                                                                On the far side was some rope and a challenge to face the minotaur… which had found Alexia and was charging towards her. It stopped after receiving an arrow to the face.

                                                                                                Henry smacked it with the flat of his blade, at which point it started crying.

                                                                                                I had been prepared to simply slay the creature, but it was just too pathetic so I commanded it to yield instead. It knelt and put its hands up.

                                                                                                A minotaur. With its hands up. God save us.

                                                                                                The Dark Lord was in his early 20s, hunchbacked and called Mark. He told us that he wasn’t much good with the forge but he had been able to create this place and hoped it would impress his father, Hephaestus, whom he hadn’t seen in six months.

                                                                                                He was very excited at the prospect of coming to join SATT, especially when they were compared to the X-Men. Berron persuaded him to put Chelmsford’s storm drains back to normal and then go on a ride on his motorbike.

                                                                                                The goblins, minotaur and dungeon disappeared and we were back above ground.

                                                                                                See also:
                                                                                                • Watling, Henry

                                                                                                A Day in the Life

                                                                                                Apr 2022

                                                                                                I’ve been making good use of the SATT training rooms since I’ve been here. It’s been a way to get to know some of the other agents while honing my swordsmanship.

                                                                                                Magnus still hasn’t recovered from the attack. It shows when he exercises and Guinevere is not cutting him any slack. He refused to repeat what she said after I stated that there was no shame in the strength of an enemy.

                                                                                                Whisper came in, took one look at us, and marched straight out again. I thought it was just me, but Magnus says she isn’t fond of him either. At the time I still had my concerns about her so dropped the matter.

                                                                                                Artie didn’t want to spar and his refusal was met by a noticeable increase in his stuttering. It’s quite obvious if you know what to look for. I didn’t press the issue and moved onto the question of the missing staff.

                                                                                                We went down to the archives, which were neatly organised, then into a second locked chamber deeper inside which were not. This looks like the area where Artie keeps the things that other people are not to be trusted with.

                                                                                                The serpent sceptre was, indeed, missing. So were a horn and a khopesh.

                                                                                                Artie was not pleased, started swearing, and grabbed a sword from the wall and proceeded to neatly destroy a table with it. He was about to put it back when he had second thoughts and strapped it on under his coat instead.

                                                                                                He then changed his mind about the sparring and agreed to meet later that evening (after, I noted, most people would have left for the day). I hope never to face that man in serious combat. His experience with the blade shows. He was a generous teacher and I learned a few techniques even from just that session.

                                                                                                The best lesson was that his style was as I had expected. It was clear that he had trained father and that Whisper had received her training from him too. I was able to relax my concerns that she might be a traitor.

                                                                                                On my way out I bumped into Ophelia who was looking for Artie. I told her I’d seen him in the archive earlier and suggested she try there. She proceeded to grill me on why I was doing leaving the office so late with wet hair.

                                                                                                I really don’t know what she thinks I might have been up to. I told her I’d been having a work out and was now going for dinner. I figured that grandfather wouldn’t appreciate his swordsmanship to be blabbed all over the office, he goes to enough lengths to keep it quiet.

                                                                                                She then invited herself to join me, an invitation I turned down because I wanted to offer Elliott thanks for his help when I was trapped and couldn’t go to Michelle’s aid.

                                                                                                So, I headed up to Elliott’s Bar. It was as busy as you’d expect a city centre pub to be on a Monday night. I started a pint while I waited for Elliott to show up, I could hear him in the kitchen from time to time. I got the impression he cares a great deal about the results that come out of there.

                                                                                                It was a nice spot I had found by the bar, with a lovely view of the main entrance where I could keep and eye on the comings and goings. These included, to my surprise, Ophelia who slipped inside, locked eyes with me, then realised she’d been spotted.

                                                                                                The interest she has in my private life has grown beyond the curious and into the outright rude.

                                                                                                She slunk off to the other side of the bar and then proceeded to spy on me while I introduced myself to Elliott properly and got talking. Apparently he feels like he knows me already given the amount of gossip he’s heard. That would explain why my ears keep burning when Michelle isn’t around.

                                                                                                We moved to the reserved table, and ordered dinner. One of the specials was gumbo and it was excellent.

                                                                                                Elliott’s magnetic personality was, at this stage, attracting a crowd of customers to general vicinity of the table. This probably annoyed Ophelia no end as they obscured her view.

                                                                                                A thin red-head wandered downstairs from behind a door marked private, cuddled up to Elliott and announced “I’m bored, aren’t you going to introduce us?”.

                                                                                                This was Morgan, and her idea of being polite is not sticking knives into people.

                                                                                                Somehow Ophelia managed to offend her shortly after Morgan left us and ended up in an arm-lock. I excused myself, hurried over, introduced them briefly and asked them not to kill each other. Ophelia claimed to be just leaving and waltzed out.

                                                                                                I left soon after, as it was getting late.

                                                                                                I’d noticed Der Ring des Nibelungen was being performed over four nights at the Vienna State Opera and asked Michelle if she fancied seeing it. I was concerned that it might be a little too close to home for her, but she announced she’d never seen it and would be happy to come with me. She was also delighted at the idea of getting a box and inviting Alexia and Berron along on a double date.

                                                                                                See also:
                                                                                                • It Happened One Night

                                                                                                A Lead to Scarab

                                                                                                Apr 2022

                                                                                                My contacts came through with a rumour that Scarab’s calling card was found at the Art Gallery Contemporary Tapiezo three days ago but no one knows what he stole.

                                                                                                It Happened One Night

                                                                                                Apr 2022

                                                                                                Yesterday and last night were a confusing mess. I’m not even going to attempt to detail everything that happened amidst all I went through. This tries to put everything that is actually relevant in an order where it is, at least, vaguely understandable.

                                                                                                While I was at Elliott’s the cameras on the 4th and 5th floors of SATT went down, and someone broke into my office and stole my gun.

                                                                                                I don’t know why. My best hope is that it is because someone didn’t trust me with a weapon and didn’t realise that it was deactivated. My nasty suspicious side says that someone ways to use it to target me with sympathetic magic.

                                                                                                Present on those floors, at the time, were Whisper, Vanessa, Julia, Frankie, and Letma. I’ll get back to them later in this entry.

                                                                                                A couple of hours later, when I’d gone to bed, Ophelia and Maggie broke into my office. They had a good poke around and stole my SATT laptop. Maggie returned it the next day. They, it seems, didn’t trust me either.

                                                                                                I got in and bumped into Alexia in the corridor and told her that I had some news on Scarab and that I wanted to brief everyone later.

                                                                                                Cue discovering the office having been entered in the night. I was not best pleased, but had no time to deal with it as I had a briefing to give.

                                                                                                Still irritated about Ophelia gatecrashing dinner the previous night, I caught everybody up on the status of the missing items, including the items Artie discovered missing from the vault the day before.

                                                                                                Ophelia raised, again, the question about where Artie had got to. She hadn’t checked the vault so, to satisfy her, we marched on down and learned that he’d left a few hours previously to get some sleep after pulling an all-nighter.

                                                                                                Henry went to check he was OK by waking him up. I don’t know why, if I was woken up three hours after getting to sleep after working all night I would not be OK.

                                                                                                My contacts had told me that Scarab was a master-thief who left a blue Faience scarab as a calling card. This wasn’t quite the same as what I had heard about SATT’s solo infiltration specialist, but it was close enough and we went digging deeper.

                                                                                                I followed up on the art theft by calling Art Gallery Contemporary Tapiezo and Berron and Alexia went to talk to Mac to try to track down his fence. He said he’d give them a call if the fence showed up.

                                                                                                My call turned up a few details, the piece that was stolen was called Soul of the Cosmos and was a modern piece that had been on display for about 6 months that incorporated outside hieroglyphics with colouration and small squares. It appeared to have been taken through the skylight.

                                                                                                Then I went and had a word with Patrizia, who was horrified at the theft (at the time I still didn’t know it was thefts, plural) and furnished me with footage from the CCTV. I’ll come back to that.

                                                                                                Meanwhile Maggie got in touch with Justin Burland about Michael. He’d cleaned out his apartment a few days before. His references for the job he had had with Burland were provided by Lex Koche of Phoenix Inc.

                                                                                                Henry, Maggie and Ophelia are going to go to New York to scour it for any sign of where he might have gone. (This is not the safest of jobs, I passed along some advice from Michelle).

                                                                                                Alexia and I cried off as we were going to Vienna this weekend. Berron looked confused. After some fumbling around we worked out that Alexia though I was going to invite him while I thought she was and we both persuaded him to come… and established that he needed to visit a tailor first.

                                                                                                Evening came and I rushed out to UCL to cover a lecture after whomever was supposed to be taking it cried off with an illness. I improvised something based on my thesis and similarities between the legends of the sword in the stone and Gram and the Barnstokkr tree.

                                                                                                It possibly wasn’t the best choice given that I saw Artie wielding Gram the previous day. It gets really awkward when mythology gets tainted by primary sources that the academic community consider impossible. Still, I glossed over that and waved a couple of practise blades about of the types that those blades may have been.

                                                                                                And so, thanks to texts from Henry and Alexia, to Mac’s — oh how I needed a drink — where I spotted Elliott (who had done something really unfortunate with his hair) at a table and Henry at the bar. I went to help him get the drinks in.

                                                                                                Berron had been upstairs with Mac and had a lead on the fence’s identity and led us over to him. With all the subtly of a brick he surprised Elliott.

                                                                                                I managed to catch on to his hints that Scarab was Morgan (also present) while the others were still hung up at the “What do you mean ‘she’?” point.

                                                                                                We reconvened at Elliott’s later that night so we could talk things through without being overheard.

                                                                                                • Morgan is a thief par excellence and uses the alias Scarab. She is not the Scarab we are looking for.
                                                                                                • Morgan is Elliott’s sister, not his lover. Maggie no longer wants to kill him for seeing someone behind her back. She isn’t best pleased that Elliott had failed to mention the existence of a sister to her until that night.
                                                                                                • I promised to show Morgan my collection of blades once I had it out of storage, and she no longer stares daggers at me for existing nearby.
                                                                                                • Ophelia promised her a trip somewhere that she could acquire a Harpy feather blade, so she no longer wants to murder Ophelia. Elliot is more than a little concerned about his sister paying a visit to Hades.

                                                                                                With that little problem cleared up, we went out separate ways. I headed back to the office to put the swords away and that’s when a few things fell into place.

                                                                                                Unfortunately they were the wrong place and I spent the rest of the night chasing red herrings.

                                                                                                The CCTV I mentioned earlier. It showed Maggie and Ophelia going up to the 5th floor around midnight. (My laptop had been returned, but Ophelia denied all knowledge of the gun claiming it was gone when she was there).

                                                                                                The CCTV for the 4th and 5th floors cut out at 10pm and came back on 10 minutes later.

                                                                                                Some hours and half a dozen coffees later I had worked out that Whisper, Vanessa, Julia, Frankie, and Letma were on the 4th and 5th floors when the cameras went out.

                                                                                                I went back to the day that the note that was supposed to be from Artie and led us to Henry arrived and established that Whisper and Vanessa were both in London that day.

                                                                                                And then I remembered that they’d both been at the Peace Talks where there was also supposed to be a spy inside SATT reporting back to the Titans.

                                                                                                %$%^*&%$%^!

                                                                                                I phoned Alexia, who wasn’t best pleased to be woken at 4am in the morning and told her I really wanted to run this by her.

                                                                                                It was circumstantial, but we agreed it warranted further investigation but also that we should check with Artie first.

                                                                                                We could hear Artie through the wall of his private office. He was shouting.

                                                                                                No don’t let him. She can’t. Please don’t hurt her. Please stop. Stop. Help her!

                                                                                                With a little advice from Alexia, I offered a prayer and blood to Britannia to help me remember the half-seen gestures Artie had used to open the door. She answered, although not in the way I expected, and the door clicked open.

                                                                                                I rushed in and shock him awake calling “Grandfather” at him and leaving Alexia somewhat dumbfounded.

                                                                                                OK, I was indiscreet. I’d been awake for coming on twenty-four hours, bounced my way around central London for most of the day, drunk my fair share of beers and then followed up with 6 or 7 cups of coffee only to find one of the only two living relatives I have who I give a damn about screaming through the wall. I wasn’t in the best place.

                                                                                                He was alright, and rather surprised that we’d got inside. He grumbled at a portrait of Britannia when I explained what had happened. I noticed that my thumb had healed from the blood offering I’d given and I now had a silver scar around the base of it. Probably best if father never finds out about that. Job 5:8-9 comes to mind.

                                                                                                I explained the suspicions I’d reluctantly come to. Artie couldn’t believe Whisper or Vanessa were involved. Eventually he came around to the idea that it was worth searching Vanessa’s office, but was adamant that Whisper was not involved and told us to talk to her.

                                                                                                Artie gave me some reassurance that I was not my father, but it was of little comfort. He trains us all to be as like him as possible and here I am following in his example and betraying him.

                                                                                                Whisper was writing a report and none too pleased to see me or Alexia. To cut a long story short, she is Lancelot, blames herself for what happened to the round table, and is more than a little unhappy to have so many reminders of Camelot at SATT.

                                                                                                Well. That explains her hostility towards me and Magnus.

                                                                                                On to Vanessa’s office, which was locked of course. I don’t lock my office and… I was robbed twice in one night. Luckily, I’d picked up a few tricks along the way and was able to get it open.

                                                                                                Her office had a general theme of ancient Egypt, including snake guardian statues which came to life and attacked us. I froze one and Alexia… incinerated the other. So much for subtlety.

                                                                                                A rapid search of the room turned up, in various filing cabinets:

                                                                                                • Shabtai is shape of Bes
                                                                                                • Girdle of Isis AKA Tyet
                                                                                                • A Was-sceptre

                                                                                                Hidden in the ceiling tiles was a coin. It is the symbol of the leader of the Hand of Isis.

                                                                                                In the SATT library we found a greek text that says:

                                                                                                Use the Was, Tyet └────┘ └─────┘ └─────┘ and the └─────┘ as part └─────┘ ceremony of rededication to your new god.

                                                                                                We reported back to Artie, who said he would blame the damage on letting a cleaner in who tripped the security systems by accident. A devious truth.

                                                                                                I went and collapsed in a chair for a few hours sleep while Alexia did some digging and found a myth claiming that it is possible to transfer loyalty and service to another god or titan. It is meant to give someone new abilities from the being who has chosen to participate in the ceremony and take them on, probably at the cost of their old powers.

                                                                                                She thinks it sounds unlikely, and is just a myth that’s got blown out of proportion but that wouldn’t explain why Vanessa would be holding artefacts supposedly needed in the ceremony in her filing cabinet.

                                                                                                I took the puzzle box to Detective Fields and asked her to dust it for prints — I owe her a favour for that, especially as she didn’t press me too hard on why — but it had been purposely wiped entirely clean.

                                                                                                Ophelia’s location potions don’t seem to work as well on non-living material, all she got from the gun’s magazine was an acrid smoke and a brief glimpse of some mountains.

                                                                                                This rather reduces our leads. I think some further looking into Julia, Frankie, and Letma is needed, although with figuring out just what the Hand of Isis is up to.

                                                                                                Alexia and I followed up with Magnus. It seems the geas still holds with him.

                                                                                                See also:
                                                                                                • Bringing the House Down
                                                                                                • Heb-Sed Festival (Special)
                                                                                                • Investigation: Rededication

                                                                                                Vienna

                                                                                                Apr 2022

                                                                                                The trip started off so well. I’d been feeling a little vulnerable without Kladenets to hand, but after we checked in there was a delivery for me. Michelle had found, or commissioned, a beautiful carbon fibre blade and had it gift wrapped. It’s a little shorter than I’m used to, but eminently concealable. It even came with a leather back holster with a wolf’s head embossed on it.

                                                                                                Das Rheingold was beautiful. The party afterwards, less so. Oh, it started out suitably fine, and the ladies got a lot of admiring looks, but then things went downhill.

                                                                                                First, Berron got curious about the mark around my thumb and I told him part of what had happened, saying the rest could wait until we were somewhere more private.

                                                                                                Next, Alexia is brought a glass of champaign by a waiter from “a gentleman”. She declines it and minutes later comes a glass of whiskey presented in the same fashion. This time the waiter tells her that it is an apology from a gentleman who has learned his lesson.

                                                                                                She declines this also and we then have to spend a few minutes explaining to Michelle that, despite what she might have heard, Taranis is not Alexia’s ex- but is her stalker.

                                                                                                Then Berron got distracted by a small creature he thought was pickpocketing guests. It didn’t respond when he called out something in gaelic but a woman — who gave her name as Susan Grey — did and he promptly spent the next 10 minutes flirting with her and returned to tell us that the creature he saw as a Kobold.

                                                                                                Later, back at the hotel we got into the whole story about how we came to be poking around in Vanessa’s office and what we found there.

                                                                                                This caused Berron to blow up over how “secretive” I am. I bristled at this, most of the secrets I keep belong to other people and are not mine to share. Michelle did more than bristle, and Alexia was none to pleased with Berron either.

                                                                                                Thanks had got tense.

                                                                                                Michelle punched Berron, who apologised… a little.

                                                                                                We retired for the night, I don’t think anyone was entirely happy. Michelle was more furious than she had let on in front of her brother and Alexia. I was more resigned to the situation, I knew that coming over to SATT would be difficult and that there would be mistrust, but I’ve worked with Berron enough that I’d hoped he would have come around by now.

                                                                                                She “was just getting to know him as family.”

                                                                                                I couldn’t stop myself pointing out that there’s nothing more like family than a brother disapproving of a new boyfriend.

                                                                                                So much for it being a fun weekend away.

                                                                                                We found a café to have breakfast at the next morning. It was heavy on pastry and delicious.

                                                                                                There were notes from our ‘friend’ Taranis who, it seems had distributed them to every café in the area to make sure that Michelle and Alexia would get them. We’ll probably keep getting them until we leave the city. That fae is getting tiresome.

                                                                                                Alexia’s was an apology for his apology. He really doesn’t understand people and I’m starting to dread the prospect of our upcoming mission to play diplomat at the Seelie Court.

                                                                                                Michelle’s was more interesting, a job offer with details to follow if she looked into a mirror and spoke his name three times. She didn’t share that with Berron or Alexia.

                                                                                                Michelle and Berron went off for a private chat and Alexia and I passed the time by speculating about what Vanessa might be up to with her collection of rededication artefacts. Our ideas got quite… exotic ranging from “She is really Michael in disguise and trying to escape his connection to the Titans” to “She is planning to forcibly remove Maggie’s connection to Athena as part of a grudge against her”. Nothing we came up with seemed remotely likely.

                                                                                                When Berron and Michelle got back, she was looking pleased with herself and he appeared to have been punched quite firmly in the side.

                                                                                                That evening we arrived at the Opera House for Die Walküre. The ladies in matching gowns, Alexia in black and Michelle in white. Since Berron was in a white suit rather than the traditional black tie I fear we may have come out looking like a chess set.

                                                                                                On our way to our box, Berron spotted the ‘pickpocket’ and gave chase. The Kobold, named Edgar, was highly offended as he was delivering messages.

                                                                                                On the subject of which, there was one in my pocket. It was an invitation to an auction to be held after the fourth night, with apologies as they had not realised I was attending. It came with a website address and password, so I passed the invitation round and took a look.

                                                                                                The auction appeared to be being run by Phoenix which wasn’t a good sign and had a rather fine collection of art. There were pictures but no descriptions, although there were minimum bids listed.

                                                                                                I recognised one piece, a Picasso, which I knew had been stolen by the Nazis. Everything else appeared to date from early enough to have been part of a WWII era horde of stolen art.

                                                                                                Given the involvement of Phoenix and the possibility of artefacts being part of the horde, my plans for a nice weekend of sharing things I enjoy with my friends — and I use the term loosely when it comes to Berron — have turned into a job.

                                                                                                I think Die Walküre was good, I confess I was a little distracted by everything else that had gone on that day.

                                                                                                I sent Maggie the details and asked her to do some digging (after some time passed so that it wouldn’t immediately be connected with the man who had been told about the website only this evening), and checking in with Artie who said that there was some budget for bidding but under the circumstances we might be better off stealing it.

                                                                                                Oh great. A heist.

                                                                                                Under other circumstances I would really love to organise a heist like this.

                                                                                                With two days notice, a team that leans heavily towards the brute force approach to problem solving, well away from my home territory and I’m less enamoured with the idea.

                                                                                                It isn’t helped by Berron’s attitude towards me. Or towards Michelle. Or towards Elliott and Morgan.

                                                                                                That was a really unpleasant fight to be caught up in the middle of. Michelle’s declaration of love for me was unexpected and horribly tempered by the argument. I was more concerned with comforting her than dealing with that.

                                                                                                My scheme to win him over with a nice four day weekend away from work is backfiring in just about every way possible.

                                                                                                Michelle and I talked for a while that night. She was less than impressed with the SATT approach of rushing in without a plan and wondered how Artie inspired such loyalty.

                                                                                                I gave away his identity. I’m still not comfortable doing that, but I want Michelle to understand me.

                                                                                                Then I had to head off any ideas of getting a sword lesson from Lancelot. Oh, the trouble that would cause.

                                                                                                She and I then had a disagreement about when SATT was founded. She swore that her mysterious boss had books on history which put the founding of SATT 200 years earlier than I thought. I’m going to have to meet this mysterious employer of hers at some point. That could be tricky though: He doesn’t like SATT.

                                                                                                That also makes it tricky for use to have an official joint mission between our two organisations, although Elliott and Morgan might be able to take some time off to help out on a personal basis. We need to discuss that with the others in the morning.

                                                                                                We could also do with figuring out what to do with Taranis. I’m getting a nasty feeling Michelle needs to talk to him in case he is mixed up in this Phoenix business.

                                                                                                Waiting in the morning was some information from Maggie.

                                                                                                She confirmed that everything in the auction has been missing since the end of the WWII. The twenty-two paintings all look normal, as does the triptych and bracelet. One of the swords, however, appears to be Kurt.

                                                                                                Wow.

                                                                                                The server hosting the website was in France, but Maggie traced it further to Hats and Feathers, a shop in Vienna at Chalbert 468. A Madam Dominique (a highly rated milliner) owns it and the shop is also her home address.

                                                                                                Breakfast consisted of a full English at The English and notes from Taranis.

                                                                                                Michelle let Alexia and Berron know about the contents of her note. This is not something to keep secret from either of them given their relationship.

                                                                                                Elliott and Morgan were still a sore spot with Berron, and it wasn’t helped by — when he eventually came round — Michelle calling them in from outside.

                                                                                                I had to chase after Berron and completely fail to persuade him to come back before he’d walked off his sulk.

                                                                                                Berron, Alexia and I went to investigate the hat shop while the others went to look around the Opera House.

                                                                                                Alexia went inside to distract the proprietor while I had a quiet look around. Berron caught the attention of a customer — whom we’d noticed at the Opera the previous night — leaving the shop and disappeared off to talk with them.

                                                                                                The whole shop was distinctly lacking in technology. Even the till was an ancient manual machine.

                                                                                                The shop floor had nothing remarkable on it (aside from the hats).

                                                                                                Downstairs were milliners supplies and a rack of servers. Lots of servers. Even I know that they were overkill for any needs this hat shop might need. There were no displays or keyboards though, so I had no way to access them.

                                                                                                Upstairs were the living quarters. There was only one thing of note: A bedroom, clearly made up for a girl, which was covered in dust and with ten or so bunches of flowers in various states of decay.

                                                                                                The account book showed regular, small, payments to an account in the name of Miss Strondel for the last 17 years. Presumably a savings account for when the child was an adult.

                                                                                                It looked very much like something had happened to the proprietress’ daughter about a year ago.

                                                                                                No sign of the art though. That must be kept elsewhere. Hopefully at the Opera House.

                                                                                                Meanwhile, Berron established that the woman he was with — Janet O’Slagan — worked for Hasenkamp. She was in town because her client — Frederic Hundertwasser — was expecting to buy several paintings at the auction and wanted them transported from the Opera House.

                                                                                                That evening we rendezvoused with the others.

                                                                                                Elliott, Michelle and Morgan had spent their time investigating the Opera House. They managed to get their hands on plans and some likely locations where the goods for auction might be being stored.

                                                                                                We made a plan to have a lot around during the intervals.

                                                                                                That’s when I received a call from Greg who wants me to appear on his TV show. I’m still not sure what happened there, beyond someone at the university giving him my name. I need to talk to him properly back in England.

                                                                                                Inside the auction house we ran into Llŷr ap Leda who clearly knew who I was, although he had the advantage over me until he introduced himself. He was here to bid on things on behalf of his mother. We were… polite at each other.

                                                                                                During the interval, Berron managed to find Jean Strondel locked away somewhere in the Opera House and spirited her away to her mother.
