                                                                                                Dominique was delighted to have her daughter restored to her, she had been kidnapped by her father who forced her to store the servers in the shop.

                                                                                                This seems like a truly bizarre way to get physical space to store some servers in. Surely it would have been less risky for them to just rent a building through a shell corporation?

                                                                                                Maggie portaled in to do a quick raid of the servers — and met active opposition which, when they determined they weren’t a match for her, triggered some sort of self-destruct which set the machines on fire. Maggie left through the portal with Jean and Dominique.

                                                                                                Back at the Opera House, Elliott called the rest of us to help with a “weird door”.

                                                                                                Alexia got waylaid on the way by Llŷr and had to spend the rest of the interval being polite until the point she he got too grabby and she resorted to punching him. With fire. Such a shame.

                                                                                                With her distracting him, we attempted to get through the door, which was very well sealed. My attempt to force it open managed to trigger some kind of magical alarm. It wasn’t fun. Happily, Morgan came along to shut it off and glare at us.

                                                                                                Elliot and Morgan raided the office for information while Michelle and I took the stairs down and found Andre preparing the items for the auction.

                                                                                                We tried to grab him so we could help ourselves but weren’t quite quick enough to stop him snatching up Kurl which immediately made us want to treat him as a friend.

                                                                                                It was infuriating.

                                                                                                He told us how to get back to the opera and we happily left. Happily until we were out of range of the effect of the blade anyway.

                                                                                                The six of us returned during the next interval and… found Andrew dead with his throat cut and Landschaft bei Paris, Paysage près de paris, Paysage de Courbevoie missing.

                                                                                                With the nagging sensation that this was a trap making the hair on the back of my neck stand up, Elliot brought the van round and we loaded up the remaining treasures and sent them off with Berron, Morgan and Elliott while the rest of us returned to the Opera to make sure we were seen.

                                                                                                The final night we went back to avoid drawing attention to ourselves. Llŷr didn’t seem to have properly learned his lesson after his treatment of Alexia the night before but he did stay out of arms length.

                                                                                                We seemed to have avoided suspicion but noted that Susan Grey was missing from the final night.

                                                                                                Back home Michelle and I talked. She is struggling with Berron, possibly more than I am. While she has many sisters, she has never really had much to do with them.

                                                                                                She summoned Taranis while I lurked out of sight. She took precautions, plenty of concealed weapons and a pot of salt (neither of us know if the legend about it is true but…).

                                                                                                After a minute her mirror shimmered silver and then formed into an image. Leather sofas, a cloak thrown across one of them, and Taranis in a dark blue shirt, cut to stop just above the end of his shortened left arm.

                                                                                                He wants Michelle to convince Berron, Alexia and their team (he struggled over the word, and you could tell he wanted to say “entourage” or “courtiers”) to meeter with him and other parties they have fought against in the past against a greater enemy. He also said that everyone would need to trust each other.

                                                                                                He paid Michelle a significant sum of money just for listening.

                                                                                                I cannot see this going well, but I have a horrible feeling we need to find out more, even if it might be a trap. Maybe I should just get Alexia very very drunk before proposing it.

                                                                                                The whole business of the hat shop sits badly with me. See the ongoing investigation.

                                                                                                I raised the Taranis issue with Maggie and she agreed that we needed to hear him out. The two of us took Alexia out and forced her to consume a significant amount of whiskey before broaching the subject.

                                                                                                Maggie was been oddly nice to me. I wonder why?

                                                                                                She was… not keen on the idea. Eventually, with Michelle’s help, we settled on a compromise where she and Berron would not go to the meeting by “send representatives” instead.

                                                                                                Michelle had managed to get herself shot (later I persuaded her to tell me about the incident, she’d gone up against the Colani Gang with Elliott and they had met much stronger resistance then they expected).

                                                                                                I took her back to the hotel afterwards and made sure to change her dressings in the morning.

                                                                                                Speaking with Artie, I learned that SATT was going to quietly use back channels to get the art back to its proper owners or museums.

                                                                                                He had similar concerns to me about the unprofessional nature of Phoenix’s operation in Vienna. Everything about it was too small scale for them.

                                                                                                Artie also had been thinking along similar lines to me about what to tell father about what I’d been up to. Berron had come to talk to him about my trustworthiness. We both thought that was something I could exploit. Oh look at me sowing strife wherever I go.

                                                                                                Father was occupied with the accounts when I arrived, so I had to lurk around the edges of his throne room getting angry looks from my sister until he was free.

                                                                                                That took much less time than usual, and he invited me to drink wine with him.

                                                                                                I seem to be rising in his estimation, it is a shame that he isn’t the type of person where that could happen if I was honest about who I was with him.

                                                                                                It seems Llŷr went crying to his mother about losing out at the auction and blamed me for it, and thus word got back to father. Now I’m going to have to ask Artie to keep the loot on ice so that I don’t get the credit for philanthropic art donations that would blow my cover.

                                                                                                Father also refused to acknowledge him as my brother. I can’t think of any other reason for Leda to have named him that way. Perhaps she kept him from father?

                                                                                                Llŷr described Michelle and Alexia as “Two of the most gorgeous women he had ever set eyes upon or ever would” and wondered how I’d got them into my employ. I put that, and distancing Berron from Alexia and the rest of the team down to father’s training. He does like to have his ego stroked.

                                                                                                I did manage to get some potentially useful information about Taranis’ movements out of him though.

                                                                                                I ran into Happy on the way out. My brother seems to be missing me, nobody else around his appreciates his jokes. He wants me to take him with me next time I leave and is eager to help with the destruction of SATT. I’ve no idea if he really means that though. He might be putting on as much of a show as I am.

                                                                                                I’ll have to see if I can find something on Midgard to busy him with, something not involving SATT and which would let me get a better feel for his real feelings and influence him away from father if need be. That won’t be easy though.

                                                                                                Meeting Taranis

                                                                                                May 2022

                                                                                                I tracked down Maggie in her library ahead of the team briefing and filled her in on what I’d learned about the kevlar. She filled in a few details and I decided I needed to see if I could go along with Alexia when she met with Detective Fields.

                                                                                                Maggie also gave me the results of the Phoenix server examination.

                                                                                                At the team meeting, Henry briefed us on his experiences with the Seelie Court and we did some general sharing of intelligence of the situation there.

                                                                                                Greg wanted to talk to Michelle so I asked her to come in and went to meet her at reception while Henry made tea. After reacting very poorly to Henry’s state of death, she gave us all a recap and we then went to meet Taranis at Mac’s.

                                                                                                Mac was not very impressed when he found out who Henry has arranged the meeting room for.

                                                                                                After getting past the “pleasantries”, Taranis explained that he wanted help with an ancient ceremony that was coming up and asked permission to bring in the other interested parties and took responsibility for their good behaviour.

                                                                                                Susan Grey arrived representing the Phoenix Library.

                                                                                                A cloaked figure representing the Hand of Isis was the other attendee. We never did see her face, but she shared an accent with Vanessa. She recoiled from Maggie.

                                                                                                Each has a coin showing their allegiance, Taranis’ was of a solar sun disc with Ouroboros wrapped around it.

                                                                                                He explained that the Seelie have an ancient pact with the Hand which requires them to assist in fighting against Apep. One of the first leaders of the Hand saved Taranis’ ancestors and they gave a life debt that is passed down to descendants in return.

                                                                                                The three chanted “The pact shall not be broken” in unison.

                                                                                                Taranis then explained about the nature of a special Heb-Sed festival. The Hand representative wasn’t happy with the level of detail he went into. They want SATT’s help in finding a couple of artefacts that went missing when Phoenix and the Hand split.

                                                                                                Maggie suggested that the items, if we found them, be kept in the safekeeping of SATT afterwards. Phoenix agreed on condition that we became signatories to the pact.

                                                                                                We were warned that children of Apophis and their minions would likely try to derail us.

                                                                                                Maggie managed to offend the Hand’s representative by calling her Travette. I’m not sure what she was thinking, if anyone is more unlikely to be an evil snake person, it is a member of the Hand.

                                                                                                Greg then offended Michelle by excluding her from the rest of the planning.

                                                                                                Sometimes I could despair.

                                                                                                Back at SATT a stone tablet was delivered to Greg with the wording of the pact.

                                                                                                Henry raided the vault for possible weapons that might fit the bill, none of them seemed to match though.

                                                                                                Greg asked me to pass on his apologies to Michelle.

                                                                                                Ophelia tracked down a mace depicting a heb-seb on public display at the Ashmolean in Oxford. After diverting Henry from a complex scheme involving setting up an exhibition which could borrow it and then stealing it in an effort to ruin Henry’s good name and insurance policy, we decided that Berron, Greg and I should just take a look at it on display.

                                                                                                Finally having a chance to talk to Greg alone, I filled him in on the situation with Vanessa and the Hand of Isis coin. He needed a stiff drink after that.

                                                                                                He checked how I was settling into SATT. Like several others, he’s worried about Berron’s antagonism. We got talking about his upcoming TV show and I got a better idea about what he wanted from me. It should be an interesting project.

                                                                                                Then we went looking for Frankie and Julia who were busy analysing matter from a tree that had been causing some problems. We asked them about what happened the night my gun went missing. They weren’t entirely honest, but we’re pretty sure the only thing they are hiding is some intra-office romance between the two of them.

                                                                                                Letma wasn’t in yet, but we found Ophelia and asked about the mountain range that she saw in the smoke from her failed potion. Greg wasn’t able to identify it but narrowed some some likely parts of the world and promised to do some digging through books.

                                                                                                We then talked about how she was setting in, talked about the upcoming housewarming, and discussed our mission to Seelie. I asked why we were needed, isn’t there a procedure? It turns out that there is, but none of the rules bring out a successor in the current situation.

                                                                                                See also:
                                                                                                • Investigation: Heb-Sed Ceremony

                                                                                                Selecting a Monarch of Seelie

                                                                                                May 2022

                                                                                                The day started well with Berron going ballistic and threatening me. I avoided rising to it while Greg talked him down.

                                                                                                While we waited, Ophelia and Maggie told us about their plan to visit the Hades Library and Henry regaled us with a talk of how he got blind drunk with Sir. Lancelot (later I’d drop Whisper a note letting her know that Henry remembered her).

                                                                                                Greg activated the mirror and we found ourselves in another realm. We were met by Furr, a herald who led us to a sunny, open area where various people were mingling. There were three clear clusters as people gathered around contenders for the thrown: Malcolm, Rose and a third party we couldn’t see.

                                                                                                Greg asked what the plan was: It was to let Greg decide through whatever means he saw fit. All usual means of determining the next ruler have been broken down (largely thanks to the lack of children), there hasn’t been a situation like it in 5000 years.

                                                                                                Kavath and Letia arrived and were overjoyed to reacquaint themselves with Henry (who it appears is not a hugger).

                                                                                                Lady Vanya was lurking in the vicinity, and not best pleased to see Berron. Henry expressed a hope that she had forgotten him and was crushed when I suggested it was unlikely given the way Kavath toasts him so frequently.

                                                                                                Greg asked Furr for his opinion on who would be contending for the throne:

                                                                                                • Malcolm
                                                                                                • Rose
                                                                                                • Vanya
                                                                                                • Mirtasha

                                                                                                We split up and had words with members of the crowd, in particular myself and Ophelia since we hadn’t acquired intimidating Fae titles. We found supporters for most of the candidates.

                                                                                                Tinanai attempted to get me under her influence when I politely kissed her hand — I resisted but it was a lesson I shall not quickly forget — and I played along.

                                                                                                Lanmorrin was a strong supporter of Kavath and Letia, despite them not having made it known that they were putting themselves forward. She said she would encourage them and that “their joy will make the Seelie better”.

                                                                                                Vanya was generally held in disfavour due to her closeness to Taranis.

                                                                                                Nem, who was as close to “one of the people” as we spoke to expressed a desire for a leader who would rule wisely and find a cure. He and his wife wanted children.

                                                                                                Maggie’s computer briefly acquired a network connection so she, Ophelia and I hurried to the mirror room to see if it had opened. Cel, princess of the Unseelie, had just arrived. This couldn’t be good.

                                                                                                Berron and Ophelia followed her to a building surrounded with dead roses where she met with Mirtasha — it was where she had made her home — and Vanya.

                                                                                                Meanwhile, I went with Henry to find Kavath. We were ambushed by Tinanai and I played the doe-eyed boy while she failed to get her little fingers on Henry. Her attempt to get past his dodging to grab him would have been comical if the possible result not so serious. When she eventually gave up and tried to lean back on me, she was peeved to find that I was not standing where she expected and that she had taken a tumble to the ground.

                                                                                                Ophelia went to investigate the roses while Berron distracted Mirtasha and her guests. She concluded they were magical, but dead (although there were very slight traces of life that might be used to coax them back), and had been killed by magic. She took cuttings for further testing.

                                                                                                They then went to Unseelie and compared the roses there to the dead ones. Unseelie roses shrunk away — possibly from the Seelie or possibly from the death surrounding them. They claimed that whatever killed the Seelie roses came from Unseelie.

                                                                                                Ophelia asked about the possibility of taking some cuttings of the roses home with her; the roses were very unhappy with this suggestion.

                                                                                                Berron spoke to Andais about the matter. She was shocked at the idea the curse came from Unseelie — the roses are blessed by the gods and it would be a crime to harm them — and that Cel was in Seelie. She dispatched Berron to bring her home.

                                                                                                Greg and various others had been manning the tent, having given until moonrise for anyone wishing to be crowned ruler to make themselves known.

                                                                                                The candidates were:

                                                                                                • Malcolm
                                                                                                • Rose
                                                                                                • Vanya
                                                                                                • Mirtasha
                                                                                                • Kavath & Letia, jointly

                                                                                                When Berron returned we went to provide backup for him. I wanted to take a look at the roses and get a sense of the magic used on them for myself. It was a good thing I did as I recognised it immediately — it was exactly like the magic that surrounded a dagger that was given to Father by his mother.

                                                                                                It was about that moment when Cel pulled a similar dagger and tried to slash Berron with it.

                                                                                                I have to confess. I expected us to take longer to find it.

                                                                                                While Cel and Berron struggled, Henry stepped in and did something that caused the both of them to cower away in fear. I took the opportunity to disarm the princess. Ophelia opened a portal back to Unseelie and Berron pulled Cel though it.

                                                                                                Once there, Cel waltzed off while Berron went to tell the Queen that she had returned.

                                                                                                Andais then went to Cel’s chambers to have a fight with her daughter. She told her mother, who relayed this to Berron, that she was manipulating the course so she could marry the new Queen — whether that be Vanya or Mirtasha.

                                                                                                That night, in Seelie, Vanya was attacked, nearly killed, and horribly scared by Mirtasha (who fled Seelie after raiding the armoury, what she took is unknown).

                                                                                                This left Vanya close to death and it was only Henry intervening to persuade Kavath to put aside their differences and heal her that saved her life. Still, her scars will take centuries to heal fully and that makes her ineligible to hold the throne.

                                                                                                While Greg listened to their answers, Ophelia and I asked some questions we had prepared to the remaining candidates (since Vanya was ineligible, Mirtasha had fled).

                                                                                                What they would do should a plague fall across their people, how they interpreted the prophecy, and what they would do given the power to wipe out an entire realm.

                                                                                                Malcolm and Rose both focused on wiping out the plague without giving any thought to protecting the people it hadn’t yet touched. Their interpretations of the prophecy were poorly thought through. And the things they would do with the ultimate power of destruction were mildly horrifying.

                                                                                                Kavath & Letia thought first of their people, were perhaps a little too quick to leap to the conclusion that they needed to sacrifice themselves to curse the curse, and were horrified at the thought of anybody having the power to destroy an entire realm.

                                                                                                Unsurprisingly, Greg selected them to be the new rulers of Seelie.

                                                                                                With that, there was just a little wrapping up to do but mostly the new rulers wanted to investigate everything we’d turned up about the curse so us visitors returned back home to get ready for Michelle’s and my housewarming.

                                                                                                The housewarming went fairly smoothly. Elliott had to be prised away from helping with the catering. Henry turned up arm in arm with Mina and Ophelia (this after pretending to be a love-sick puppy all day: I do not understand that man’s sense of humour). There were numerous gifts.

                                                                                                Michelle forced me to make a speech, so, unprepared as I was, I reached out for the first thing that seemed appropriate and quoted Henry Van Dyke:

                                                                                                Every house where love abides
                                                                                                And friendship is a guest,
                                                                                                Is surely home, and home sweet home
                                                                                                For there the heart can rest.

                                                                                                Later, I went looking for Berron and well. I basically begged him to trust me. We seem to have made some progress.

                                                                                                He ended up playing some songs, and he sounds even better life. Dicky surprised me by turning out to be an enormous fan of his.

                                                                                                See also:
                                                                                                • Watling, Henry

                                                                                                Sally and the Kevlar

                                                                                                Jun 2022

                                                                                                Alexia and I went to meet Sally at a coffee shop to collect an example of the kevlar that has been causing us problems of late.

                                                                                                She brought it in a backpack and left it by the table. A beautifully executed classic drop-off.

                                                                                                We exchanged information on the Colani gang to further our investigation. She didn’t know much but will have words with Organised Crime to see if she can learn anything.

                                                                                                Afterwards, we took the armour back to SATT to perform some tests. They didn’t go well. Alexia lost control of her magic wearing it and set her office on fire, and just being near it disrupted Henry’s ability to summon his sword to the point that it appeared flying through the air and I had to dodge and grab its hilt to stop it cutting my head off.

                                                                                                We took a trip to Wales to show it to Jaxom in person and got his input on it — the short version being that it should be so difficult to make that it shouldn’t exist.

                                                                                                Henry took the Kevlar then, he is going to pass it on to Hephaestus. Jaxom asked him to take a horn along too (and seems to be treating it as a big joke; hopefully the forge god won’t shoot the messenger.)

                                                                                                See also:

                                                                                                  Henry in Flames

                                                                                                  Jun 2022

                                                                                                  It was supposed to be a simple team briefing to get everybody up to date. I’ve been sitting on my report on the Heb-Sed business until Greg had had a chance to tell Maggie about Vanessa’s relationship with the Hand.

                                                                                                  While we were waiting for everyone to turn up (Alexia and Berron turned out to be very late indeed) to the meeting, Henry and I went off to find Artie who was reportedly rather grumpy.

                                                                                                  Patrizia was less than happy to see Henry, which gave me hope that the source of Artie’s displeasure wasn’t my uncovering of the aforementioned troubles with Vanessa. I helped sweep up some broken sea shells while she stared daggers at Henry.

                                                                                                  Knocking on Artie’s door we received similar greetings and Artie informed Henry that his ears were bleeding. It turns out that Aphrodite got into an argument with another god about Henry — possibly over the relationship between him, Ophelia and Mina — and then took out her displeasure on Artie.

                                                                                                  In good news, Henry is no longer a simple consultant but is officially on secondment from his knightly duties to SATT, with Greg as his supervisor, for the next year. He gets the office next to mine and some paperwork (and my help with it).

                                                                                                  Artie and I briefly chatted about my plans to visit Sam; he was concerned about what father might think, but I have all the justification I need lined up already.

                                                                                                  With the meeting finally starting, we discussed the Kevlar business (Berron has an insight into one of the mirror visions, and Henry told us that he has passed the Kevlar and horn along to Hephaestus).

                                                                                                  Next up was the Heb-Sed situation. We agreed to the plan where Berron, Greg and I would go to Oxford to take a look at the mace.

                                                                                                  Henry, on behalf of the trio, invited everyone to a ball at his place at some point in the summer, and I received an email from Whisper so I passed along the invite to him.

                                                                                                  Thank you. I apologise for being so harsh towards you. It’s hard as this is all so painful. But I appreciate you letting me know about Henry. I will see him. Would you like to come along? If i can take the step toward talking to you I can, I can maybe consider talking to Artie. W

                                                                                                  There was nothing new on the Verdas front and the meeting broke up after that.

                                                                                                  I was telling Greg about my intention to go and see Sam and he asked if he, as Sam’s opposite number, could join me. I said I’d see if I could arrange it.

                                                                                                  And then the screams from down the corridor came. We followed them to Greg’s office where Henry was on fire with black flames coming from what seemed to be his heart.

                                                                                                  It took the combined efforts of Alexia, Berron and me to douse the flames.

                                                                                                  Greg ran for a media and Ophelia and I tried to help Henry get more comfortable. We saw a vision.

                                                                                                  In it, Henry was holding a different sword and saying “You shall not have them!”. He fought a creature, melted his sword almost down to the hilt in the process, but continued to strike at it. The creature forced him to the ground tearing at his chest, he burned his hands, then forced the remains of the sword through the creature’s forehead. Then he was crawling towards a door. There were bright lights and a dark figure and then death.

                                                                                                  For some reason, the vision made me think of the dragon in Beowulf. It was a sheer gut feeling and I can’t figure out what brought it to mind.

                                                                                                  Someone, Berron I think but it was rather chaotic, wasn’t pleased that I blurted out “Was that what happened to Alexia’s parents?!”. It turns out that, for all the help I’ve been giving Alexia with the Verdas investigation, the rest of the team think that the geas is still there, albeit weakened, and needs protecting.

                                                                                                  With Henry recovered enough to no longer be screaming, we learned what had happened. He had taken his shirt off to show Maggie the scars on his back and chest when Berron came in. He took a look at them and saw a knot of “grubby, dirty magic that exploded into flames” in the scars.

                                                                                                  It’s a spell type that, if it doesn’t kill the target, waits until it can. It’s a very deep and black magic of the worst kind. It is supposed to persist until death but, in Henry’s case, well beyond that.

                                                                                                  We got Henry back into the conference room.

                                                                                                  Artie arrived lugging a full length mirror for Greg. Patrizia arrived shortly after with a matching hand mirror for Alexia. They had been made Ambassadors to he Dragon Court.

                                                                                                  Henry felt he owed Berron a debt for using his power against him and Cell in Seelie and insisted that he owed Berron a boon. Berron was reluctant to accept, but I pointed out that since Henry’s honour demanded it he should accept it for Henry’s sake. Reluctantly he did and a tattoo of Berron’s axe appeared on Henry’s arm.

                                                                                                  Is this what it means to make a deal with Fae?

                                                                                                  Berron then picked a fight with Ophelia, it seems he was unhappy with the lack of care she took in Unseelie and he is still having to deal with the fallout. I wonder if he also needed a new target for his displeasure after we made the beginnings of peace the other night?

                                                                                                  After he’d finished shouting and failing to accept Ophelia’s apology, he flounced off, calling Artie “father”.

                                                                                                  Which makes a horrible kind of sense.

                                                                                                  And which also makes Berron my uncle.

                                                                                                  I have a feeling that a family Christmas may get very complicated.

                                                                                                  Later Alexia dropped by my office. She wanted to know what I had seen and complained about Berron and Maggie wrapping her in cotton wool. I refused and pointed out, in no uncertain terms, that this was about protecting the geas and not her.

                                                                                                  She persisted claiming that it wasn’t the same thing. It was, however, perilously close and I told her that she needed to back off and let the rest of us deal with it. It isn’t worth risking everything that she arab, Click, Magnus and Bad Moon sacrificed.

                                                                                                  She stormed out. So that went well.

                                                                                                  About ten minutes later I heard screaming from next door. Alexia and Ophelia were there and Henry was on fire again. I desperately tried to put the fire out, but Berron wasn’t there to help with his axe and it took longer.

                                                                                                  When they were finally out I ran to my office to make sure a medic was on the way. I also wanted to be away from Alexia before I said something I’d regret. She couldn’t leave it well alone, could she?

                                                                                                  When the medics arrived I filled them in on what had happened. Maggie turned up and went to check on Alexia who had hidden herself in her office. Ophelia took Henry home, which I thought was for the best.

                                                                                                  The Alexia shouted for me, demanding to know why I didn’t tell her what I had seen. As if I hadn’t explained myself already.

                                                                                                  She said that the vision was the same as Artie’s nightmares, which let a couple more pieces fall into place and my Beowulf theory suddenly began to take on a glimmering of logical consistency.

                                                                                                  Beowulf’s dragon was slain by a hunting party that included Sigmund who ate its heart. There may have been something about black flames being involved. Of course, Sigmund was the wielder of Gram who drew it from the “tree” and Gram is now in the possession of Artie.

                                                                                                  We then went round in a circle of Alexia wanting to know more and everyone else wanting to protect the geas. It was… frustrating.

                                                                                                  Maggie and I went out for coffee to catch up. We decided we really needed to talk to Artie about it and arranged a meeting.

                                                                                                  See also:
                                                                                                  • Sherwood Story

                                                                                                  Acquiring the Heb-Sed Mace

                                                                                                  Jun 2022

                                                                                                  These things just can’t be simple. What was supposed to be a nice little junket to reconnoitre a possible artefact in a museum turned into a chaotic heist.

                                                                                                  The drive down was bad enough, Berron had finally twigged that Michelle had moved in with me and was griping about how I hadn’t told him.

                                                                                                  We found the mace without much trouble and confirmed that it was a powerful artefact, and that should have been the end of it, at least for the day.

                                                                                                  However, on the way out we discovered an anxious museum employee getting ready to ship it to (as Berron discovered having lunch with her) a lab in Oxford for a round of x-rays and MRIs. Our old friends Hasenkamp were doing the shipping.

                                                                                                  Awkward, but not critical.

                                                                                                  Meanwhile Greg was pumping employees in the cafeteria for information and learned from a couple of disgruntled ones that the mace was being shipped off to UCL for their new miracle process.

                                                                                                  Two different stories, and the plot is starting to stink of week old fish.

                                                                                                  While we made plans, we took a tour and found some other items of interest.

                                                                                                  Greg got permission from Artie to do whatever was needed to secure the mace, Berron and I went to check out the transport.

                                                                                                  After icing up the door so it didn’t close properly behind someone leaving, we went in. Berron distracted the van’s driver while I went to stick my phone under the bumper (GPS enabled).

                                                                                                  To make things more complicated, I found someone else’s (certainly not Hasenkamp’s — it wasn’t fitted properly for an official job) and removed it, sticking it behind a drain pipe on the building so it wouldn’t move too much and alert whomever was monitoring it.

                                                                                                  When the mace was moved, Greg went to bring the car around while I took our mystery tracker and threw it in the back of a passing open-top rubbish truck. Whomever was wanting to keep an eye on that vehicle was going to have an exciting trip to Redbridge household waste recycling centre.

                                                                                                  Meanwhile, we followed the Hasenkamp van to London City Airport. It seemed that the mace was being taken out of the country. We had to move fast.

                                                                                                  While one of the people in the van was busy in the terminal, we headed for the van.

                                                                                                  While Berron seduced the driver’s door open and then punched him out, I took the brute force approach and shattered the passenger window, dodged the bullet, then grabbed his gun arm and pulled with enough force to smash his face against the door frame and make certain he would need dental work in the near future.

                                                                                                  Taking my victim’s weapon and wallet — Raymond Grant who I traced to a fruit shop along with 32 other fake IDs — and retrieving my phone from where I’d stuck it, we stole the van and drove for 10 minutes before changing vehicles and driving back to SATT (since there was a lack of room with the mace in the car, Berron went back via Unseelie).

                                                                                                  Given the missing artefacts — and Maggie’s extreme paranoia about them — we stashed the mace in lockup B with a camera monitoring it, then put a box with a weight in it in lockup D (again, with a camera), and filed paperwork saying it was in D.

                                                                                                  See also:
                                                                                                  • Watling, Henry
                                                                                                  • Investigation: Heb-Sed Ceremony
                                                                                                  • Heb-Sed Mace

                                                                                                  Sherwood Story

                                                                                                  Jun 2022

                                                                                                  Aphrodite provided Mina with a spell that she said could unentwine Artie and Henry (so that Artie would stop reliving Henry’s deaths).

                                                                                                  We travelled to a spot near Edinburgh where Henry had died while protecting Helen and George. We found there an odd moss which Berron examined using his powers. I took a sample for analysis.

                                                                                                  It caught fire.

                                                                                                  This is becoming a theme.

                                                                                                  Henry gave a gasp of pain, causing Berron to turn around and look at him.

                                                                                                  Henry caught fire.

                                                                                                  I emptied a fire extinguisher we’d stolen from our hotel over him.

                                                                                                  Berron and a couple of the others went off to examine the house while Henry stayed well away.

                                                                                                  Mina cast the spell that Aphrodite have provided her with.

                                                                                                  What I hadn’t realised was that the spell was supposed to “help unravel the threads of the story”. This turned out to be a lot more literal and figurative — yes, I’m aware that sounds like nonsense — than Henry and Mina expected.

                                                                                                  And so we found ourselves in Sherwood Forest, just down the road from Nottingham. Most of us were dressed in Lincoln Green, with the notable exceptions being Greg in a friar’s cassock, myself in scarlet, and Ophelia in leather with an apron.

                                                                                                  And when I say “we”, I include Artie and Alexia, despite us leaving them in London.

                                                                                                  We did all still have our wits about us, and our abilities still worked. There was one exception: Mina, in the role of Robin Hood (one arm in a sling and unable to fire a bow), was appeared to believe she was the character and told us that we needed to defeat the Sheriff.

                                                                                                  We appeared to been dropped in the traditional story of the golden (sometimes silver, but golden in this case) arrow. The Sheriff was running the archery competition and we worked on the theory that we needed to acquire the arrow to complete the spell.

                                                                                                  Robin, her arm in a sling, was naturally unable to take part in the competition so that role fell to Alexia (in the guise of Little Joan) and Ophelia who went to sign up.

                                                                                                  Meanwhile Greg used his religious regalia to go in and see the prisoners, whom we had spotted on a poster advertising their execution after the competition — the Sheriff was clearly applying the belt and braces approach to luring Robin out of hiding — and looked disturbingly like Magnus and Scarab.

                                                                                                  Scarab was confident he could free himself, but wasn’t so sure about Magnus. They developed a plan in which we would ambush the guards when they were escorted out for the execution.

                                                                                                  Outside, while the archery competition took place, I was approached by someone looking remarkably like Jerry who recognised me as Will Scarlet. He solicited a bribe from me in exchange for arranging for the portcullis to fail to close and for horses to be waiting outside.

                                                                                                  He also told me that the Sheriff’s plan was to pre-empt any attempt to win the contest and escape with the goods by arresting both archers who made it through to the trick-shot round.

                                                                                                  And so it was that everything kicked off. Things were… chaotic.

                                                                                                  I didn’t see most of what went on, but I cut down a couple of guards before they could reach Greg while he orchestrated the release of Magnus and Scarab.

                                                                                                  Then I ended up in a fight with the Sheriff in which he found it unsurprisingly difficult to use proper legwork while standing on a patch of ice — I know it was a beautiful fictional summer, but this is me and my powers were still working.

                                                                                                  The least said about Ophelia’s contribution to the fight the better. Apparently she can hurl lightning… but isn’t proficient at aiming it. Ouch.

                                                                                                  It ended when Magnus came to help, lost his footing, and knocked the Sheriff into my blades.

                                                                                                  He cried out “My father will revenge me! Verdas!” as he died.

                                                                                                  Meanwhile Maggie grabbed the golden arrow in time for us to leap onto horses and ride off.

                                                                                                  Working on the assumption that, when we got out of this realm, we’d all go back to where we were, I took advantage of the change to talk to Scarab to find out what had happened to him.

                                                                                                  He was in a jail cell in Egypt — we would later narrow this down to Amarna — after he had been knocked on the head by somebody with super-strength and bound in unbreakable chains by someone (who, unhelpfully, wore a mask) who could make them liquid and twist them. He had been thrown on a boat and taken to Egypt. The messages sent through Apollonet has been sent by a friend, he doesn’t have access to the geas is still in effect.

                                                                                                  He also explained the Ares craved the horn of the wind and had sent several people to try to steal it from Thoth.

                                                                                                  Back at the outlaw camp the arrow was hung from a tree and we feasted. Reality returned.

                                                                                                  The moss which had covered Henry’s death site had shrivelled up and turned grey. The sample in the packet in my pocket included.

                                                                                                  The house we were near appeared to be more decayed and not particularly habitable. There was the flicker of a TV still on in an upstairs window though.

                                                                                                  I found a key under the doormat and we went inside. It was rather run down, just like the outside. The most noticeable features were a vast collection of pictures of Boscastle (where Verdas had imprisoned his wife) and a roughly human-shaped pile of mulch — matching the remains of the moss outside — in front of the television.

                                                                                                  Based on how lived in the house was, and the receipts we found, it looks like Charlie (if that is who it was) arrived at about the same time as Henry’s curse started to flare up.

                                                                                                  See also:
                                                                                                  • Boscastle
                                                                                                  • Lancelot

                                                                                                  Boscastle

                                                                                                  Jun 2022

                                                                                                  Since the aftermath of the last mission pointed firmly towards Boscastle, we decided to head there to see what we could find out about The Great Bardess of Cornwall.

                                                                                                  The pre-mission briefing also revealed that Artie seemed to be avoiding Berron and Henry. I resolved to track him down and find out why when we got back. For some reason Ophelia’s mother is under the impression that Ophelia is dating a son of Ares, which is curious.

                                                                                                  We also got an explanation for Henry’s grumpiness: Aprodite is worries about infiltrators at SATT so he is trying to lure out them out by appearing to be disgruntled and ripe for recruiting.

                                                                                                  Berron still wanted to examine the kevlar, and found that it appeared the colour of old blood under his magic-detecting sight. Ophelia gave her location potion a shot and it blew up, this time Greg got to see the vision and was able to identify the location we could see in it.

                                                                                                  When we arrived in Cornwall, we split up. My group headed to the Witch museum to see if we could dig up anything useful from local history. Berron and Greg headed to the castle to examine the site.

                                                                                                  There they discovered Willapark Lookout, built by one Thomas Rickard Avery, radiating magic.

                                                                                                  Meanwhile at the museum we found that there was to be an opportunity for people to join the Gorsedh Kernow; Ophelia was keen to get Berron to take part.

                                                                                                  We managed to find a genuine book about magic and I learned that grandmother was taught to craft legendary items and weapons by The Wyvern.

                                                                                                  We were kept busy going through the material until the others rejoined us.

                                                                                                  On the way out I spotted a familiar face in the crowd. It was my bother Happy.

                                                                                                  Taking my leave from the team, I followed him to Boscastle Inn. He was carrying a parcel, about the size of a book, under one arm. When he arrived at the inn he passed it to the barman and ordered a drink.

                                                                                                  I slid into the booth next to him and was treated to an outburst of disgust about how father had sent me to keep and eye on him. I quickly reassured him that it was just coincidence that I was here and asked him how he was doing.

                                                                                                  He wasn’t enjoying the lager, so I suggested he try an ale next time. He had no idea what was in the package — no surprise there, for all father names us after himself and trains us to be like him, the old bastard never trusts us with the details.

                                                                                                  Henry had tracked down the Great Bardess’ ghost which was haunting the coastline at dawn and dusk. He learned that her power comes from her voice and that she was trapped by the crystals that hurt her husband because she “had looked on his true form and would have revealed it to the world”.

                                                                                                  She said she would do everything in her power to defeat Verdas is she was freed. She thought that the local bards were trying to sing the crystals out.

                                                                                                  We monitored the inn through its fire. The parcel was collected by a weasel-faced man, so I dashed to be nearby so I could follow him. Unfortunately, he headed towards a car so I had to act quickly. Taking on the role of a drunk rolling out of pub after drinking a little too much right after work, I bumped into him and completely failed to slip Maggie’s tracker onto the package. I stumbled back against the car and tried to stick it to the underside. Still no luck.

                                                                                                  Remaining in character, I lurched onwards and disappeared into the shadows of a nearby ally. Then I turned around and burst the passenger side rear tire with shards of ice to stop him leaving.

                                                                                                  He made a call to Pinel le Savage to say he would be late and returned to the inn.

                                                                                                  Later, we he was about to leave, Maggie and I jumped him from behind, snatching the package along with his wallet, watch and phone to sell the story that it was just a coincidence rather than targeting the book. Someone wandered out of the pub, took one look at Maggie, muttered “Lizard?” and wandered back inside. Hopefully they’ll put it down to the drink.

                                                                                                  The rest of the team had gone to another pub to meet the Bards.

                                                                                                  The proceedings were quite ritualised with masks being handed out, Berron used his senses on them and saw them, the people wearing them and the entire room dripping in evil magic. It’s possible his powers still need a bit of practise.

                                                                                                  After they each gave a reading, Henry and Alexia were invited to join the circle and they all began to read some poetry.

                                                                                                  At this the package on the table between Maggie and I began to vibrate. I ripped the package open. It was a copy of The Grand Grimoire: The Red Dragon.

                                                                                                  Using the book as a guide, Maggie and I were about give Henry and Ophelia enough information for them to help the lead Bard make a blood offering and shatter a piece of tourmaline that was used in the ceremony.

                                                                                                  A woman in green emerged and after greetings was done with, enquired about her children. She was shocked at what they had been done and didn’t believe it until Henry showed her his cursed scars. She said that “This cannot be allowed to stand”.
